Multi-Teacher Contrastive Distillation for Lightweight Plant Disease Classification
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Lightweight deep models offer a promising avenue for real-time plant-disease recognition on edge devices, yet their accuracy often degrades under stringent compute budgets. We propose CropKD, a resource-aware classification framework that synergistically integrates three neural-computing components: (i) a lightweight multi-scale feature fusion module (LMFF) that enriches spatial representation via parallel depth-wise convolutions and channel-wise attention; (ii) a multi-teacher adaptive distillation strategy (MTAD) that dynamically fuses complementary knowledge from convolutional and vision-transformer teachers; and (iii) a contrastive knowledge distillation loss (CKD) that tightens intra-class embeddings while enlarging inter-class margins. Extensive experiments on FGVC8, BARI-Sunflower and DiaMOS show that CropKD achieves state-of-the-art accuracies of 94.5\%, 98.99\% and 94.11\%, respectively, while retaining only 4.5 M parameters, 0.6 GFLOPs, 2.8 GB RAM and 95 W power. On a Jetson Nano it runs at 36 FPS, demonstrating real-time deployability under true field conditions. The results validate CropKD as a generic recipe for compressing heavy vision transformers into ultra-light edge-intelligence models, and provide a practical tool for sustainable smart agriculture. Code, pretrained weights and splits will be made publicly available.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Multi-View Dual-Contrastive Graph Learning with Adaptive Agreement for Semi-Supervised Text Classification
candidates.abstract: Text classification with few labeled examples requires models that can effectively exploit unlabeled data while remaining lightweight. Graph-based approaches address this by modeling documents through their relations, but existing graph contrastive methods for text often rely on augmentations that alter semantic structure and are affected by unreliable false negatives. We propose Multi-View Dual-Contrastive Graph Learning (MDCGA), a framework that learns a shared document representation by integrating lexical, semantic, and keyword-based relational signals through enhanced dual contrastive objectives designed to reduce the impact of false negatives. Experiments on MR, Ohsumed, AG News, and R8 show that MDCGA achieves accuracies of 85.71%, 70.49%, 92.76%, and 97.40%, respectively. The approach demonstrates robustness in very low labeled settings, uses relatively few parameters, and shows limited sensitivity to hyperparameter choices.

candidates.abstract:
<jats:p>The process of gathering useful information from online messages has increased as more and more people use the Internet and other online applications such as Facebook and Twitter to communicate with each other. One of the problems in processing online messages is the high number of noisy texts that exist in these messages. Few studies have shown that the noisy texts decreased the result of text mining activities. On the other hand, very few works have investigated on the patterns of noisy texts that are created by Malaysians. In this study, a common noisy terms list and an artificial abbreviations list were created using specific rules and were utilized to select candidates of correct words for a noisy term. Later, the correct term was selected based on a bi-gram words index. The experiments used online messages that were created by the Malaysians. The result shows that normalization of noisy texts using artificial abbreviations list compliments the use of common noisy texts list.
 </jats:p>

PatientPheX: A Full-Text Biomedical Corpus for Patient-Specific Phenotype Information Extraction
candidates.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                <jats:p>Patient-specific phenotype information extraction identifiers and normalizes phenotype entities and links them with individual patients, supporting rare disease research and genotype-phenotype analysis. However, existing datasets rarely combine full-text biomedical content with detailed annotations of patients, phenotypes, related entities, and their associations. In this work, we present PatientPheX, a corpus for patient-specific phenotype information extraction comprising 200 full-text articles, primarily case reports and case series. The corpus provides mention annotations and normalization for seven biomedical entity types, together with explicit associations between patients and entities across sentences, paragraphs, and sections. Negated findings and composite phenotype mentions are also annotated. Corpus construction combines automated pre-annotation, large language model (LLM)-assisted verification, and manual review and adjudication. Benchmarks cover entity recognition and normalization and patient–phenotype association extraction using gold-standard and predicted entities. The overall document-level entity F1 was 86.95%, while phenotype F1 was 79.33%. The best relation extraction macro-F1 decreased from 84.14% with gold-standard entities to 54.98% with predicted entities, highlighting the combined challenges of phenotype extraction and patient attribution. PatientPheX provides a resource for developing and evaluating patient-centered information extraction methods and supports the construction of structured patient-level knowledge resources for phenotype-driven biomedical research.</jats:p>

candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Protected least-sufficient reconstruction (PLSR) is applied to a codimension-three timelike Codazzi defect with a primitive projective link and two non-scalar source grades. Exact marked recovery selects E3 ⊕ E2 and M3(C) ⊕ M2(C). Primitive multiplication unifies the projective exact sequence, the rigid (2, 3) correspondence, its Green metric, the minimal rank-five Hermitian carrier, and a structural dark port line. Centered determinant/Clifford completion gives S(U(3) × U(2)), the primitive Z6 quotient, chiral 16-plets, and kY = 5/3; the integral A2 branch gives the three-state family orbit and primitive commensurate norm-seven class. One Alena-Codazzi response supplies typed realization tests. Its finite realization combines the upstream source/local incidences with three executable packets: a marked four-moment primitive-port certificate, a control-basis-invariant scalar/trace susceptibility residual, and a common-root holonomy test whose remaining primitive-root lift is one Z2 bit. After the stated exact reduced attachments, the scale-free response is a one-dimensional saturation manifold with global coordinate u and a discrete norm-seven orientation. One predeclared scale-free observable may locate u; the remaining continuous CKM, PMNS, neutral-shape, and bosonic coordinates are no-retune tests. Absolute normalization, continuum poles and lifetimes, and precision matching remain separate completion problems.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Protected Reconstruction from Codazzi Defects: Equianharmonic Quantization and a Minimal Standard-Model Carrier
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>A geometric reconstruction framework is developed in which protected data of a codimension-three timelike Codazzi defect determine both a finite internal structure and a constrained low-energy prediction manifold. Protected least-sufficient reconstruction selects a primitive $3+2$ carrier, its multiplication and dark-line geometry, the global form $S(U(3)\times U(2))$, a chiral $16$-dimensional coefficient packet with $k_Y=5/3$, and a norm-seven family structure. These data are embedded in a single Alena-Codazzi Parent action. Its conserved charge provides an intrinsic selector $\chi_Q=dQ/d\Omega$; directional bounds, Fredholm-Feshbach reduction, and validated continuation give sufficient conditions for a unique first protected constrained fold without assuming global charge convexity. The selected Parent state fixes a single scale-free coordinate $u_*$ and simultaneously determines a rank-one critical-response residue that can be recovered from stable-side data with certified second-order error. This gives independent tests of the critical direction, its transport into family and dark sectors, and proposed causal relations between them. The resulting charged-family shapes form fixed-Casimir $A_2$ circles, while norm-seven and contraction-Wilson data organize hierarchy and CP orientation. Spectral states and dark-channel widths are treated separately through Schur-Herglotz, Hankel, and outgoing-channel tests. After one global calibration, electroweak, charged-family, CKM, and Dirac-PMNS observables are constrained to a one-dimensional no-retune manifold. Absolute normalization, Majorana data, and continuum scattering remain independent completion problems.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Prototype-guided semantic transferability for reliable knowledge distillation in brain tumor MRI classification
candidates.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains challenging due to subtle inter-class differences, imaging variability, and uncertainty in model predictions. Although deep learning models achieve strong performance, their complexity limits deployment in resource-constrained settings, making knowledge distillation a practical approach for transferring knowledge to lightweight student models. However, conventional distillation methods typically assume uniform teacher reliability and often overlook semantic structure and prediction reliability. To address this limitation, we propose a prototype-guided semantic transferability framework that selectively transfers knowledge based on predictive confidence and alignment with class prototypes in an embedding space. The method introduces a prototype memory to capture class-level structure and formulates a transferability score to adaptively weight the distillation process. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in classification performance, calibration, robustness, and cross-dataset generalization while preserving the efficiency of the student model. Ablation studies, statistical analysis, and feature space visualizations further support the effectiveness of the proposed components. Overall, the proposed framework aims to enhance knowledge distillation by incorporating semantic structure and uncertainty, leading to more reliable and discriminative representations without additional inference overhead.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Q-Conditioning and Q-Gating: Metadata-Driven Attention Mechanisms for Medical Vision Transformers
candidates.abstract: Background: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have demonstrated efficacy in visual recognition tasks through global dependency modeling via self-attention. However, standard ViT architectures lack native mechanisms for integrating external clinical metadata (e.g., patient demographics, lesion characteristics, image quality indicators) into the visual processing pipeline, limiting their utility in multi-modal diagnostic scenarios. Methods: We propose two novel attention mechanisms: Q-Conditioning and Q-Gating, designed for efficient metadata fusion within the transformer framework. In Q-Conditioning, metadata is projected into the query space and added to the query vector, guiding attention toward contextually relevant regions during early computation. In Q-Gating, a learned gate modulates computed attention scores, enabling soft, differentiable control over token interactions. We further introduce a hybrid attention framework wherein standard, Q-Conditioning, and Q-Gating heads coexist within the same model. Results: We evaluated our approach on four medical imaging benchmarks (PAD-UFES-20, TissueNet, PH2, and NDB-UFES). Specific configurations, particularly Q-Gating and hybrid variants (e.g., QC_QG, QG_S), achieved &gt;95.5% accuracy on PAD-UFES-20 and &gt;92% average score on PH2, significantly outperforming image-only baseline models (p&lt;0.001). On TissueNet, where auxiliary inputs consist of PhikonV2 foundation-model embeddings rather than raw clinical metadata, all configurations exceeded 99% accuracy; however, we note that these gains are substantially attributable to the pretrained encoder and are reported separately from the primary clinical-metadata claims. Attention concentration metrics, encompassing both theoretical conditional entropy reduction and empirical absolute entropy dispersion, correlated strongly with diagnostic performance gains (&rho;=0.89), indicating improved focus on diagnostically salient regions while avoiding spurious attention collapse. Conclusions: Metadata-aware attention mechanisms enhance both performance and interpretability in domains where auxiliary information is critical. This work provides a scalable extension to ViTs that supports multi-input modeling while preserving architectural integrity and computational efficiency.

candidates.title: Rafale: Towards the Efficient Resource-Aware Federated Knowledge Distillation on Heterogeneous Clients
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Knowledge distillation is an highly effective machine learning technique for transferring knowledge from a large model, i.e., teacher, to a smaller model, i.e., student, improving model efficiency without sacrificing performance. This paper proposes a novel resource-aware federated learning framework Rafale that incorporates an adaptive client clustering mechanism based on computational resource availability and model complexity. High-resourceb clients train complex teacher models, and low-resource clients leverage distilled knowledge from teachers to train lightweight student models. Further, to optimize the aggregation process by introducing a clustering-based weightsharing mechanism that minimizes communication overhead while maintaining model accuracy. In this paper, a revolutionary Rafale framework that greatly reduces communication cost and separates model training from architectural constraints is proposed. To increase scalability and robustness, the suggested method makes use of resource-aware client selection, adaptive information sharing, and effective distillation techniques. In comparison to state-of-the-art FL approaches, experimental data show that RA-FKD delivers greater accuracy, decreases communication costs by up to 76%, and improves system efficiency. A cosine similarity loss KDC is introduced in knowledge distillation to improve the alignment between teacher and student models, enhancing knowledge transfer. Experimental evaluations on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets demonstrate that proposed framework achieving student test accuracy of 91.15% with reduction of 76.08% communication cost.</jats:p>

Real-Time Markerless Motion Capture for Interactive Applications and Game Engines: Pipelines, Spatio-Temporal Refinement, and Latency Budgets
candidates.abstract: The rapid evolution of deep learning and computer vision has transformed markerless motion capture (MoCap) from specialized biomechanical tools into a key technology for real-time interactive systems, video game engines, and virtual production. This review analyzes state-of-the-art markerless pipelines and focuses on integrating 3D human pose estimation (HPE) into standard graphics engines. We evaluate the shift from single-view regression to temporal convolutional architectures. Our review emphasizes the trade-offs between spatial precision and algorithmic overhead for interactive use cases. Central to our analysis is the spatio-temporal refinement of noisy skeletal data. We assess adaptive smoothing techniques, such as the 1-Euro filter and predictive neural filtering, designed to minimize jitter and motion-to-photon latency. Findings indicate that modern markerless systems approach the standards of marker-based tools. However, maintaining temporal consistency under strict real-time budgets remains a fundamental challenge for human-display feedback loops. We examine industry-standard engines and their role in permitting seamless character retargeting throughout diverse applications, including clinical monitoring and sports coaching. Ultimately, this work synthesizes methodologies to optimize the responsiveness of AI-based MoCap systems within contemporary real-time software architectures.

candidates.title: Reliability in Emotion Classification, Sentiment Analysis, and AI-Generated Text Detection: A Systematic Review
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Text classification systems are increasingly deployed in settings where a confident but incorrect prediction carries a real cost. Aggregate accuracy on a held-out split says little about whether such a system can be trusted. This systematic review examines how reliability is pursued and evidenced across emotion classification, sentiment analysis, and AI-generated text detection. Following PRISMA, seven electronic databases (ScienceDirect, Scopus, Web of Science, ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, Compendex, and PubMed) were searched together with a supplementary Google Scholar search. The search covered text-only journal articles and conference papers published from January 2016 through July 2026 that addressed a relevant NLP task and evaluated or improved at least one reliability dimension. Of 1,797 records identified, 1,294 were screened after deduplication, 464 were assessed in full text, and 51 studies met all criteria. Each study was characterized using a five-dimensional taxonomy: Task Category, Model Type, Reliability Approaches, Reliability Evaluation Evidence, and Reliability Validation. Task Category is mutually exclusive; the remaining four dimensions are non-mutually exclusive. Dataset language was recorded separately. Across the 51 included studies, AI-generated text detection accounts for 28 studies, sentiment analysis for 15, and emotion classification for 8. Encoder-Based Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs) are the most common Model Type (35 studies), followed by Decoder-Based LLMs (25) and Other Deep-Learning Architectures (18). Reliability Approaches are led by Uncertainty Estimation (15 studies), followed by Selective Prediction (9), Calibration (7), Distance and Representation Methods (7), Statistical and Likelihood Methods (5), and Consistency and Agreement Methods (3). Their distribution differs sharply by task category: Under the operational coding definition used in this systematic review, Uncertainty Estimation appears in 12 sentiment studies and 3 emotion studies, while no AI-generated-text study met the criteria for this category. All 5 Statistical and Likelihood Methods studies occur in AI-generated text detection, a concentration that partly reflects the category definition, since likelihood-based provenance statistics are themselves a detection technique. Reliability Evaluation Evidence is most often Error-Rate and Operating-Point Evidence (19 studies), followed by Calibration Evidence (14), Selective Prediction and Coverage Evidence (10), and Uncertainty Evidence (9). Reliability Validation is also uneven: 24 studies include Out-of-Distribution Validation, 21 Adversarial and Perturbation Validation, 20 Cross-Generator Generalization, 4 Cross-Lingual Validation, while 18 are limited to In-Distribution testing. The review 2 contributes a unified five-dimensional framework that makes the application, model context, reliability mechanism, supporting evidence, and validation conditions directly comparable across the three task categories and exposes where evidence remains narrower than the reliability claim it is used to support.</jats:p>

candidates.abstract: <jats:p>This research focuses on enterprise profiling in scenarios where large volumes of diverse texts—such as registration records, annual reports, news articles, and bidding notices—are continuously generated. Instead of relying solely on a single data representation or classification model, we developed a comprehensive natural language processing (NLP) pipeline for extracting key information and identifying industries. The pipeline consists of several steps. First, we use a BERT-BiLSTM-CRF model to identify core e/nterprise entities. Then, we combine TF-IDF with BERT embeddings to create a hybrid feature scheme that captures both lexical cues and contextual semantics. To address the challenge of imbalanced industry labels, we apply SMOTE in the dense semantic space and pair it with Focal Loss to enhance learning for minority classes. Additionally, we introduce a Stacking strategy to integrate outputs from different models, making predictions more stable. Tests on a self-compiled dataset covering ten national economic sectors and about 50,000 enterprises show that our method achieves a macro-F1 score of 95.4%. It outperforms traditional machine learning baselines and single deep learning models, offering more reliable recognition for minority classes. These results suggest that our framework is well-suited for applications such as supply chain partner discovery, industrial mapping, and targeted investment promotion.</jats:p>

Sequential Shared-LoRA Adaptation of BERT for Text Classification: A Continual-Learning Baseline
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Fine-tuning a pre-trained language model separately for every classification task is costly in computation and storage, and scales poorly when tasks arrive over time. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) reduces this cost, but whether a single shared adapter can serve several classification tasks trained one after another remains underexplored. We study a frozen BERT-base backbone with one shared LoRA adapter in its self-attention layers and lightweight task-specific heads, trained sequentially on three tasks derived from the aclImdb movie-review corpus: binary sentiment, a rating-bucket task derived from the 1–10 review ratings, and a heuristic five-class genre task built from keyword rules, since the corpus has no genre metadata. The adapter and heads together comprise 302,602 of 109,784,842 parameters (0.2756%), cutting estimated storage for three tasks by 66.5% relative to per-task full fine-tuning. Each task peaks immediately after its own training stage (sentiment 88.6%, rating 89.1% against a 50% majority baseline, genre 57.2%). Sequential training, however, causes measurable forgetting: sentiment accuracy falls monotonically to 81.7% (forgetting score 0.0697) and rating accuracy from 89.1% to 83.5% (0.0550). These single-run results show that a compact shared adapter can support several related tasks while exposing interference under sequential adaptation, and they provide a reference accuracy–retention trade-off against which architecture-, regularization- and replay-based continual-learning mitigations can be evaluated.</jats:p>

candidates.title: SFE-Mamba: A Spatial&ndash;Frequency Collaborative Enhancement Network for Object Detection in Snowy Road Scenes
candidates.abstract: Snowflake occlusion, reflections from accumulated snow, and low-contrast imaging in snowy environments can degrade target features and impair road-object detection performance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes SFE-Mamba, a snowy-weather object detection network built on Mamba-YOLO. First, a Snow Spatial&ndash;Frequency Feature Extraction Stem (SSF Stem) is designed to jointly model target features through dual spatial- and frequency-domain branches. The frequency-domain information is decomposed into low-, mid-, and high-frequency components and adaptively weighted, thereby preserving target structural information while suppressing frequency disturbances caused by snow particles, snow cover reflections, and illumination variations. Second, a Snow-Aware Mamba Attention Block (SMA Block) is developed by integrating local structural modeling, two-dimensional selective scanning, and Multi-Dimensional Perception Self-Attention (MPSA). This design strengthens the interaction between local details of weak targets and long-range contextual information, improving feature representation under occlusion and low-contrast conditions. Finally, Focus Convolution (FConv) is introduced to reduce the loss of target edges, textures, and positional information during scale transformation. Experiments were conducted on the real-world snowy dataset Snow-ACDC and the simulated snowy dataset Snow-VOC. SFE-Mamba achieved mAP50 values of 74.2% and 71.8% on the two datasets, respectively, outperforming the Mamba-YOLO baseline by 3.6 and 3.9 percentage points. Compared with CF-YOLO, a detector specifically designed for snowy scenes, SFE-Mamba further improved the mAP50 by 1.6 and 1.8 percentage points on the two datasets, respectively. The model contains 6.8 M parameters and reaches an inference speed of 58 FPS. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively improves object detection accuracy in complex snowy road scenes while maintaining a favorable balance between detection performance and computational efficiency.

candidates.title: SmolVLA-Diff: efficient knowledge distillation for VLA models for vertical task deployment
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>This paper systematically compared the high performance π0 model with the high efficiency SmolVLA model. Real machine evaluation revealed that π<sub>0</sub> relying on its powerful flow matching action of generator and huge VLM model number, precision lead in vertical task; While SmolVLA through lightweight attention head and asynchronous reasoning stack, on delay, power consumption and anti-jamming advantage is obvious. In order to integrate the advantages of the two models, we innovatively propose an action knowledge distillation method at the output layer to transfer the action strategy knowledge of the π<sub>0</sub> model to SmolVLA, so that it can obtain similar performance improvement to the former with negligible additional overhead. This study provides an effective performance enhancement scheme for the efficient and practical deployment of the robot VLA model.</jats:p>

candidates.title: SSKD-Depth: Spectral–semantic Knowledge Distillation for efficient monocular depth estimation
Stage-Aware Optimization of Llama 3 Model Inference for Language Services on Many-Core CPUs
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>LLM-based language services (e.g., summarization, translation, and question answering) require low-latency and cost-effective inference, yet GPU resources may be costly, unavailable, or difficult to integrate in many deployments. Many-core CPUs provide a flexible alternative, but achieving efficient inference requires optimizations that match the distinct computational characteristics of the Prefill and Decode stages. This paper presents a stage-aware optimization approach for Llama 3 inference on two Phytium many-core processors (FT-2000+/64 and FT-1500A). Fine-grained profiling shows that matrix-vector multiplication (MVM) in the Decode stage accounts for 99.4% of Decode time, whereas Prefill exposes additional token-level parallelism. Accordingly, in Prefill we reorganize multiple token-wise MVM operations into matrix–matrix multiplication and select the GEMM implementation by micro-batch granularity, including a blocked C GEMM (up to 7.8× over token-wise MVM) and a LibShalom-based tile path. In Decode, we apply OpenMP-based intra-kernel parallelism to MVM, RMSNorm, Softmax, and attention-head computation. Experiments on representative GLUE workloads show that the self-kernel implementation improves time per output token (TPOT) by 1.67× at two threads (2.80× at eight). A complete baseline study then shows that a tuned BLAS GEMV accelerates the dominant Decode MVM by a further 3.1×; following the stage-aware selection principle, the final configuration reaches a TPOT of 141.9 ms—a 17.2× end-to-end speedup (7.05 tokens/s per 16-core node)—with scaling that continues to all cores. A kernel-level scalability study on Phytium FT-2000+/64 (Decode MVM up to 8.4× at eight threads) further shows that saturation beyond eight threads is a property of the kernel implementation rather than of the platform. These results demonstrate that stage-aware characterization and per-stage implementation selection can substantially improve single-request Llama 3 inference efficiency on many-core CPUs, and provide guidance for CPU-side optimization in language-service deployments.</jats:p>

Systematic Comparison of Electroencephalography Feature Domains for Visual Stimuli Decoding with EEGNet and EEG Conformer
candidates.abstract: Electroencephalography-based visual decoding has important applications in brain&ndash;computer interfaces and cognitive neuroscience, yet the relative effectiveness of different feature extraction methods for sustained visual paradigms remains unclear due to the absence of standardized, multi-dataset comparative evaluations. This study systematically compares eight feature extraction methods across three public EEG datasets: MindBigData MNIST, MindBigData MNIST-8B for digit recognition, and MSS for natural image classification. The methods include coherence, Granger causality, directed transfer function, partially directed coherence, transfer entropy, discrete wavelet transform, empirical wavelet transform (EWT), and wavelet scattering transform. Two deep learning architectures, EEGNet and EEG Conformer, were trained using two pre-processing pipelines, with and without artifact removal. EWT achieved the highest classification accuracy, reaching 97.83% for digit-vs-blank and 77.10% for within-session natural image classification. Connectivity-based methods consistently underperformed, with the best connectivity method (coherence) reaching up to 91.67%, suggesting that spectral power information is more discriminative than inter-channel relationships. Cross-subject generalization remained challenging, with best accuracies near 68%. The findings establish wavelet-based adaptive spectral decomposition as a strong baseline for EEG visual decoding and highlight the need for domain adaptation techniques to address cross-subject variability.

candidates.title: Systematic Review as Recipe Book for Nuanced Emotion Detection in Noisy Text
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Recognizing emotion in informal text at the granularity mental health support requires, telling nervousness from fear or remorse from sadness, remains far below usable accuracy: five years of work on Google’s GoEmotions multi-label 28-emotion dataset has reached only .5475 macro F1, and no systematic review has examined why. Accurate emotion recognition is an important predictor of mental healthcare success, yet its subjectivity makes it difficult for even trained human annotators to agree on nuanced emotions in noisy text. Our systematic search identified 494 papers. Inclusion required the full 28-emotion dataset, deep learning models, and reported macro F1, yielding 30 papers and 71 models. Among the highest-scoring models, 9 of the top 10 employ explicit emotion-learning architectures or objective functions. We found no LLM-based models exceeding the foundation paper’s baseline performance. Only 5 of the 71 models underwent extensive hyperparameter tuning. We attributed the observed ceiling to tuning practice as much as architectural limits. Systematic reviews are rare in AI/ML relative to medicine. This scarcity, combined with a submission surge that has outpaced peer-review capacity, plausibly explains why the field’s true state-of-the-art result went unrecognized for years. This recipe book details the emotion-specific design and tuning techniques associated with the strongest results. The strongest results in the corpus are associated with combining explicit emotion-learning architectures, objective functions, and rigorous tuning, though the reviewed models remain well short of the performance likely needed for practical usability in mental healthcare. Current evidence does not support LLMs as a competitive alternative.</jats:p>

candidates.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper investigates an efficient approach for distilling Large Language Models (LLMs) into smaller, application-specific models using zero-shot Chain of Thought (CoT) rationale generation and Optimization by Prompting (OPRO). To address the challenges of deploying computationally intensive generative AI for narrow tasks or resource-constrained environments, the approach leverages LLM reasoning capabilities to generate both labels and natural language explanations for unlabeled data. By reducing reliance on human-generated annotations, the approach substantially lowers annotation requirements and prompting costs while maintaining comparable performance in the evaluated settings. We formulate distillation as a multi-task learning problem in which student models are trained to jointly predict labels and learn from teacher-generated rationales, with the goal of improving data efficiency and generalization. Building on established zero-shot Chain of Thought (CoT) prompting and the OPRO prompt optimization technique, we use teacher-generated rationales to reduce annotation token requirements and examine the associated performance and efficiency gains. Additionally, we systematically investigate how explanation properties affect distillation efficiency. Across natural language inference and question answering benchmarks, results indicate that near-optimal performance can be achieved even when rationales are provided for only a subset of the training data, and that shorter explanations are often sufficient. These findings provide practical insights into the trade-offs between rationale generation cost and student model performance. Overall, this work contributes empirical evidence on the effectiveness and cost characteristics of rationale-based distillation for training compact, task-specific language models with minimal human intervention.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Toward the Dynamics of the Spiral Structure Model: Canonical Quantization, Core Electrodynamics, and the Defect Propagator
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>The Spiral Structure Model (SSM) describes the photon as a helical quantum and the electron as a ℤ₂ topological vortex defect of an elastic covariant medium, but its published account is kinematic: the medium’s dynamics was recorded as an open problem. This companion paper reports a concrete candidate dynamics and four derived results. Canonical quantization of the Goldstone (circulation) sector yields an exactly solvable one-quantum problem whose virial theorems return [x, p] = iħ and the SSM momentum width Δp_x = mc/√2. A phase-locking mechanism between the internal circulation and a ξ-scale core texture supplies the two-scale charge structure of the SSM, reduces the self-energy problem by four orders of magnitude, sharpens the core-size bound to ξ ≲ 1.4×10⁻¹⁹ m, and renders the internal excitation band electromagnetically dark (spectral weight ~ 6×10⁻¹²). The gauge sector of the candidate action is QED at one loop, so Schwinger’s a₁ = α/2π is inherited with a definite core-scale deviation; the defect propagator is assembled to the point where its residual failures are quantitative diagnostics rather than open searches; and the elastic vertex follows from the core current with a profile-independent charge radius r_ch = ξ and, for the texture-gradient profile, a diffraction zero at 0.56–4.0 TeV. Finally, the full constraint set on the locked core leaves a global survival window (a factor 65 in the locking stiffness, with walls set by collider and g−2 bounds) and Lorentz covariance of the one-quantum reduction, the one structural gap, is closed: the retarded self-energy kernel supplies (2/3)E₀ of the texture’s inertia where the instantaneous kernel supplies none, the frame-field stress, fixed by the Derrick identity of the soliton sector as the Poincaré-stress analog, supplies the remaining (1/3)E₀, and the von Laue criterion then gives the exact dispersion E(v) = γE₀. The residual open items, the quantum completion of the internal tower and the interaction vertices, are stated with their exact locus of failure.</jats:p>

Universal Noise Augmentation (UNA): A Unified Training-Time Framework for Robust Multilingual Text Classification
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Reliable multilingual text classification systems must tolerate surface-level noise without losing clean-input performance. Existing robustness toolkits provide perturbation libraries and evaluation workflows, but they do not by themselves define a compact training-time protocol that jointly controls perturbation scope, severity, sampling, and clean-noisy exposure. We introduce Universal Noise Augmentation (UNA), a unified training-time framework that integrates character-, token-, and structural-level perturbations with configurable intensity, clean-noisy mixing, operator sampling, and epoch-aware dynamic resampling. UNA is a protocol-level contribution rather than a claim of new primitive corruption operators, and it requires no modification to the classifier architecture or loss. We evaluate UNA with XLM-RoBERTa-base in three multilingual classification settings: cross-lingual natural language inference (MultiNLI→XNLI), intent classification (MASSIVE), and sentiment classification (Amazon Reviews Multilingual). Evaluation separates clean data, an in-family synthetic-noise stress test, and fixed task-specific noisy subsets, and includes ablations of intensity, clean-noisy ratio, sampling strategy, and dynamic versus static augmentation. Across six noisy task-tier comparisons, UNA improves accuracy by 6.8–8.5 percentage points, while clean accuracy changes by at most 0.4 percentage points. The results support UNA as a practical, architecture-preserving robustness-training configuration for engineering multilingual classification pipelines under the evaluated conditions.</jats:p>

candidates.title: When Quantization Preserves Accuracy but Not Evidence: Explanation-Aware Post-Training Quantization for Medical LLMs
XBRIDGE: Cross-Domain Bridge Distillation for Data-Efficient Video Classification
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Compact video classifiers often underfit on small, domain-specific datasets, while mismatched pretraining sources can limit direct knowledge distillation. We propose Cross-Domain Bridge Distillation (XBRIDGE), which transfers knowledge from a teacher through an assistant pretrained on a semantically adjacent video domain to a compact student. On XD-Violence, a Kinetics-400 assistant achieves higher standalone accuracy (86.26%) but produces a weaker student (68.39%) than a cross-domain Something-Something V2 assistant (72.95%). This suggests that assistant accuracy is a poor proxy for transfer quality and motivates investigating temporal and object-interaction priors for low-data targets. A lightweight Contextual Bridge Optimiser supports assistant and supervision-weight selection under a fixed compute budget. Evaluation on binary violence detection and multiclass sports recognition shows gains over direct fine-tuning and direct distillation. We report parameters, FLOPs, and latency alongside classification performance to characterise the trade-offs for compact video transformers.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Zero-Inflated Asymmetric Rate-Distortion Quantization: Risk-Aware Mixed-Precision Online Inference for Real-Time Tax Revenue Forecasting
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Timely tax revenue forecasts support fiscal planning, yet deploying probabilistic forecasting models in operational systems requires a difficult balance between predictive fidelity and computational speed. That balance is particularly consequential when tax collections contain frequent zeros, extreme values, and economically unequal consequences of forecast errors. This study develops a zero-inflated asymmetric rate-distortion quantization framework for mixed-precision inference with a pretrained quantile Temporal Fusion Transformer. Its objective combines an asymmetric Huber-based quantile penalty, a zero-revenue penalty, and additional weight on distributional tails. A primal-dual controller adjusts numerical precision across model units in response to recent filing patterns and a profiled latency constraint. The source manuscript reports normalized distortion values of 0.734 and 0.762 for the proposed method on its value-added-tax and FRED-derived evaluation streams, respectively, compared with a uniform-quantization reference of 1.000; its reported latency-feasibility rate is 0.981. These values are reproduced here as reported, not independently validated; the source does not supply executable code, complete provenance of the underlying data, or hardware benchmark logs. The proposed approach offers a testable route toward aligning inference resources with fiscal forecasting risk, but replication and deployment-level validation remain necessary.</jats:p>

Comparative analysis of image augmentation methods for improving the quality of computer vision models in animal husbandry
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>The research is aimed at developing robust computer vision models for precision animal husbandry tasks (health monitoring, animal identification, and body condition scoring), which are commonly hampered by a scarcity of labeled data. Collecting and annotating images in real-life farm conditions is an expensive and labor-intensive process. Data augmentation methods are a key solution for expanding training sets and improving the generalization capability of models. This paper examines several methods for preprocessing cattle image data and explores augmentation methods that use the pre-existing data to generate new data and enrich training data without human intervention, thereby enhancing performance. The experiments have addressed various aspects of data scarcity, yielding competitive results that provide a baseline for future research.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Efficient Glaucoma Detection from Retinal Fundus Images Using a Lightweight DeiT-Small Vision Transformer and Test-Time Augmentation
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Glaucoma is one of the major causes of permanent blindness in the world, and since the progressive nature of the disease leads to considerable damage of the optic nerve before diagnosis, there is a need to develop precise and effective automated screening tools. This paper suggests the implementation of a lightweight vision transformer network for glaucoma screening based on the DeiT-Small architecture. The images were downsized to 224 × 224 resolution and transformed into patches. Four transformer blocks were frozen while the other blocks were fine-tuned via layer-wise learning-rate decay (LLRD) along with data augmentation and Test-Time Augmentation (TTA). Testing was performed on a balanced dataset with 9,540 images: 8,000 for training, 770 for validation and 770 for testing. In the independent test dataset, the model achieved 91.65% accuracy, 91.55% F1-score, 91.56% sensitivity, 95.06% specificity, and 95.84% AUC-ROC. candidates.title: GLaDViT: interpretable gated fusion of frozen vision, text and layout features for document image classification
candidates.abstract: Classifying scanned pages by document type is a routing step in enterprisedocument processing. Layout-aware models reach high accuracy but rely onlarge-scale document pretraining and full fine-tuning, and seldom expose why adecision was made. We study a deliberately lightweight alternative, GLaDViT,which keeps CLIP and BERT encoders frozen, derives a layout descriptor fromTesseract hOCR word boxes, and trains only a gated fusion head. Because theclassifier is linear in the gated sum of modality embeddings, every class logitdecomposes exactly into per-modality terms, which yields an attribution that isfaithful to the computation by construction, unlike the gate weights alone. Ona label-corrected release of Tobacco-3482 (2737 pages, fixed 2186/272/279split), GLaDViT reaches \((93.7\pm0.4%)\) accuracy over three seeds (95% Wilsoninterval 90.2--96.0%), against 87.7% for the best single modality; addinglayout to vision and text contributes 2.8 accuracy points and gating a further1.1. The layout stream nevertheless receives at most about 10% of the gatemass, indicating that gate weights are mixing coefficients rather thanimportance scores. A triple InfoNCE alignment of the three streams, used as awarm-up on frozen features, lowers accuracy to 90.3%; we analyse this negativeresult. Code and hOCR tooling will be made publicly available.

SANet: lightweight geometry fusion for adaptive robotic grasping
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Real-time object perception with geometric awareness is a critical enabling technology for intelligent visual perception in robotics. However, deploying robust visual recognition on resource-constrained edge devices remains challenging due to computational limitations and the lack of geometric priors. This paper presents a lightweight technology framework that integrates an improved AlexNet-based dual-branch network (SANet) with dilated convolutions and a geometry-informed loss function, enabling simultaneous object classification and geometric property inference from a single forward propagation. Unlike conventional end-to-end grasping methods, the proposed framework emphasizes system-level technology integration: it fuses RGB appearance with noise-free STL geometric priors during training, then discards the auxiliary branch at inference to maintain a low computational footprint suitable for embedded platforms. Experimental validation on a humanoid robot for automated manipulation tasks demonstrates high recognition accuracy (93–97%) and stable operation across varying object appearances, with an end-to-end processing time under 0.31 s on a consumer-grade GPU. The work provides an efficient, interpretable, and geometry-aware solution that advances intelligent perception technologies in robotics and automation.</jats:p>

candidates.title: SOP-DETR: a lightweight end-to-end detection model for small object detection in UAV aerial images
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Small-object detection in UAV aerial images is difficult for two practical reasons: the targets are small, dense, and easily blended into complex backgrounds, and the detector still has to run with limited computation at the edge. We propose SOP-DETR, a lightweight end-to-end detector built on RT-DETR-R18. The model uses a Dynamic Multi-Scale Context Mixing Module (DMSCM) to improve weak-texture representation, a Small-Object Enhanced Feature Pyramid (SIP-OmniFPN) to inject P2 details into P3 fusion through SPDConv and CSPOmniKernel, and a Multi-scale Cross-scale Feature Modulation Module (MCFM) to replace fixed concatenation with adaptive feature selection. On VisDrone2019, SOP-DETR reaches 38.8% mAP@0.5, 22.1% mAP@0.5:0.95, and 13.8% APs, which is 3.7, 2.1, and 2.7 percentage points higher than RT-DETR-R18. It also reduces parameters from 19.9M to 14.8M and GFLOPs from 57.0 to 53.1. On TinyPerson, SOP-DETR obtains 22.5%, 7.9%, and 6.3% on the same metrics, improving the baseline by 2.2, 3.9, and 1.3 percentage points. Ablation studies and visual results show that the three modules improve small-object representation while keeping a practical balance between accuracy and efficiency.</jats:p>

AgentScope 1.0: A Developer-Centric Framework for Building Agentic
  Applications
candidates.abstract:
Driven by rapid advancements of Large Language Models (LLMs), agents are
empowered to combine intrinsic knowledge with dynamic tool use, greatly
enhancing their capacity to address real-world tasks. In line with such an
evolution, AgentScope introduces major improvements in a new version (1.0),
towards comprehensively supporting flexible and efficient tool-based
agent-environment interactions for building agentic applications. Specifically,
we abstract foundational components essential for agentic applications and
provide unified interfaces and extensible modules, enabling developers to
easily leverage the latest progress, such as new models and MCPs. Furthermore,
we ground agent behaviors in the ReAct paradigm and offer advanced agent-level
infrastructure based on a systematic asynchronous design, which enriches both
human-agent and agent-agent interaction patterns while improving execution
efficiency. Building on this foundation, we integrate several built-in agents
tailored to specific practical scenarios. AgentScope also includes robust
engineering support for developer-friendly experiences. We provide a scalable
evaluation module with a visual studio interface, making the development of
long-trajectory agentic applications more manageable and easier to trace. In
addition, AgentScope offers a runtime sandbox to ensure safe agent execution
and facilitates rapid deployment in production environments. With these
enhancements, AgentScope provides a practical foundation for building scalable,
adaptive, and effective agentic applications.

candidates.title: Very Large-Scale Multi-Agent Simulation in AgentScope
candidates.abstract:
Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have opened new avenues for
applying multi-agent systems in very large-scale simulations. However, there
remain several challenges when conducting multi-agent simulations with existing
platforms, such as limited scalability and low efficiency, unsatisfied agent
diversity, and effort-intensive management processes. To address these
challenges, we develop several new features and components for AgentScope, a
user-friendly multi-agent platform, enhancing its convenience and flexibility
for supporting very large-scale multi-agent simulations. Specifically, we
propose an actor-based distributed mechanism as the underlying technological
infrastructure towards great scalability and high efficiency, and provide
flexible environment support for simulating various real-world scenarios, which
enables parallel execution of multiple agents, centralized workflow
orchestration, and both inter-agent and agent-environment interactions among
agents. Moreover, we integrate an easy-to-use configurable tool and an
automatic background generation pipeline in AgentScope, simplifying the process
of creating agents with diverse yet detailed background settings. Last but not
least, we provide a web-based interface for conveniently monitoring and
managing a large number of agents that might deploy across multiple devices. We
conduct a comprehensive simulation to demonstrate the effectiveness of the
proposed enhancements in AgentScope, and provide detailed observations and
discussions to highlight the great potential of applying multi-agent systems in
large-scale simulations. The source code is released on GitHub at
https://github.com/modelscope/agentscope to inspire further research and
development in large-scale multi-agent simulations.

candidates.title: Kronos: A Foundation Model for the Language of Financial Markets
candidates.abstract:
The success of large-scale pre-training paradigm, exemplified by Large
Language Models (LLMs), has inspired the development of Time Series Foundation
Models (TSFMs). However, their application to financial candlestick (K-line)
data remains limited, often underperforming non-pre-trained architectures.
Moreover, existing TSFMs often overlook crucial downstream tasks such as
volatility prediction and synthetic data generation. To address these
limitations, we propose Kronos, a unified, scalable pre-training framework
tailored to financial K-line modeling. Kronos introduces a specialized
tokenizer that discretizes continuous market information into token sequences,
preserving both price dynamics and trade activity patterns. We pre-train Kronos
using an autoregressive objective on a massive, multi-market corpus of over 12
billion K-line records from 45 global exchanges, enabling it to learn nuanced
temporal and cross-asset representations. Kronos excels in a zero-shot setting
across a diverse set of financial tasks. On benchmark datasets, Kronos boosts
price series forecasting RankIC by 93% over the leading TSFM and 87% over the
best non-pre-trained baseline. It also achieves a 9% lower MAE in volatility
forecasting and a 22% improvement in generative fidelity for synthetic K-line
sequences. These results establish Kronos as a robust, versatile foundation
model for end-to-end financial time series analysis. Our pre-trained model is
publicly available at https://github.com/shiyu-coder/Kronos.

candidates.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
candidates.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) aims to transform interaction experience into persistent improvements, yet external feedback is costly and world-model predictions may become unreliable as policies evolve. We introduce RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework built on JEPA-Anything that uses predictive world models to guide action and learning-data selection. Observed feedback drives policy or workflow improvement and conditional world-model adaptation, while component and compatibility checks govern the retention of updated policy-model pairs. Across diverse computational and scientific domains, RSI-Anything demonstrates substantial gains. In code repair, with the coder fixed, success increases from 26.3% with a static verifier to 29.2% through predictive selection and 31.2% after world-model adaptation, at comparable test usage. Graphical user interface (GUI) evaluations showed higher task completion, while average actions decrease by 39.4%. Across five successive policy versions, laboratory-planning scores more than double from 21.80% to 46.01%. In reaction optimization, RSI-Anything achieves 96.15% mean best observed yield versus 82.16% for Bayesian optimization under the same 40-experiment budget. An end-to-end immune-science application further connects workflow evolution and predictive modeling with therapeutic hypothesis generation. These results demonstrate how predictive world models and retained system updates enable recursive improvement across diverse environments.

candidates.title: Build, Don't Play: Self-Improving LLM Research Agents Develop a Hearthstone Battlegrounds AI That Rivals Top Players
candidates.abstract: Can LLM agents carry a hard real-world problem from raw data to a system that holds its own against people? We study this in Hearthstone Battlegrounds, an eight-player auto-battler with stochastic shops and battles, hidden information and nearly a thousand interacting cards. We present AutoTavern, a self-improving research system: specialised LLM research agents share a typed research memory, every claim passes verification gates, and live games close the loop, so the agents improve the simulator, opponents and policy and, from the same feedback, their own research process; a human sets goals and rules on ambiguous mechanics. In 20 days AutoTavern built TavernGym, the first faithful, full-content reproduction of the live game, and delivered 23 versions of TavernAgent, trained with PPO against opponents calibrated to real games. TavernAgent plays complete games on the live ladder by itself: its rating rose from 6,000 to about 15,000 and, on the public leaderboard's measure, its last 20 records average a placement of 1.60 with 80% first places, better than the server's ten highest-rated players on every statistic (2.34, 59%). TavernBench, 960 tasks in 40 scenarios, shows that the system the agents built is the strongest player: TavernAgent answers 91% of the play tasks against at most 63% for frontier LLMs, and decides in 0.03 s where they need up to 26 s; within the second a live turn allows, it keeps 90% and no LLM more than 26%. LLM agents build far better than they play. We will open-source TavernBench and TavernGym at https://github.com/MCG-NJU/AutoTavern. Applicability review: AI-driven development and software engineering agent evaluation.

candidates.title: MOSS-Image Technical Report
candidates.abstract: Recent closed-source image generation systems can produce diverse visual content from simple compositions to information-dense graphics, yet open-weight text-to-image models still struggle with dense text and intricate layouts. To narrow this gap, we introduce MOSS-Image, an open generation system that combines high-fidelity visual synthesis with intent-aware composition. First, we pretrain a 5B single-stream diffusion transformer (DiT) from scratch with a carefully designed recipe, enabling bilingual long-form text rendering and precise layout control. Second, we develop an intention-aware agentic prompt enhancement (PE) module that translates diverse user requests into detailed content and layout specifications. Together, they enable MOSS-Image to generate text-rich and layout-coherent images. We further introduce LongLongTextBench (LLTB) for evaluating long-form English and Chinese text rendering, and RealLayoutArena (RLA) for end-to-end layout-rich generation. MOSS-Image achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-weight models on LLTB, with an average text coverage of 96.3%. On RLA, MOSS-Image ranks second in the end-to-end system comparison, while its backbone ranks first among generators evaluated with shared enhanced prompts. We will release the model, training recipe, and evaluation framework to support further research and promote the text-to-image community.

candidates.title: YuE2: Unifying Symbolic and Audio Music Generation at Frontier Quality
candidates.abstract: Symbolic models make melody, harmony, rhythm, and form explicit but typically stop before a finished recording; audio models produce complete songs while leaving composition implicit. We introduce YuE2, which unifies symbolic and audio music generation at frontier quality through symbolic planning. A single AR-NAR Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) first writes a readable score specifying melody and harmony, expands it into semantic music tokens, and realizes it as full-song audio. In comparisons using the same checkpoint, experts prefer symbolic planning for overall quality and musicality, with 49.3% of overall preferences versus 34.6% without planning. Experts also favor the unified model over a separate language model and diffusion Transformer. On WildSongBench, YuE2 scores 6.73 on SongBench Global Avg, exceeding all evaluated public baselines. Selecting from eight candidates (best-of-8), YuE2 reaches 6.96, the highest observed mean among all evaluated systems. Expert listening further establishes its competitiveness with proprietary song generators, favoring best-of-8 over Suno v4.5 and yielding nearly balanced preferences against Suno v5. To learn this generation process from recordings without aligned scores, we introduce MERT2 and SheetSage2 to supply semantic and symbolic supervision. MERT2 sets a new state of the art in music representation learning, surpassing previous best results on 14 of 15 MARBLE metrics; SheetSage2 leads 12 of 15 benchmark-metric pairs in our lead-sheet transcription comparison. The same checkpoint follows score edits while largely preserving unedited musical content and generates zero-shot covers without cover-specific training. Its readable score also enables agentic music editing, with external language models translating user feedback into revisions of the composition.

candidates.title: nanoMuse: An Open-Source Personal Agent for Every Device You Own
candidates.abstract: Assistants from 2011 answered and waited, and agents from 2023 did a task and stopped. In September 2026 Meta's Muse showed an agent for one person, with accounts, devices, memory and a conversation that lasts, closed, in a vendor's cloud, in one country. Such an agent is expected to act on a person's accounts and devices, remember them across weeks, speak first when it is worth it, and answer for what it did. It is a kind of software, not a model, and until now had no open counterpart. This report defines the personal agent in five questions and three horizons. It reads how Muse is built from Meta's public record and a copy of its production prompt, each statement marked by its source. It then presents nanoMuse, the open-source counterpart under the GPL-3.0, one agent on every device a person owns, with hands on the phone's screen and the computer's. They share one conversation over a relay anyone can run; every action goes through a Sentinel, memory is files the person can read, and the model is their choice. Its size and cost are given as estimates. What is open, memory with provenance, an evaluation suite for the hands and an open model for them, is set out as a roadmap.

candidates.title: Bitnet.cpp: Efficient Edge Inference for Ternary LLMs
candidates.abstract:
The advent of 1-bit large language models (LLMs), led by BitNet b1.58, has
spurred interest in ternary LLMs. Despite this, research and practical
applications focusing on efficient edge inference for ternary LLMs remain
scarce. To bridge this gap, we introduce Bitnet.cpp, an inference system
optimized for BitNet b1.58 and ternary LLMs. Given that mixed-precision matrix
multiplication (mpGEMM) constitutes the bulk of inference time in ternary LLMs,
Bitnet.cpp incorporates a novel mpGEMM library to facilitate
sub-2-bits-per-weight, efficient and lossless inference. The library features
two core solutions: Ternary Lookup Table (TL), which addresses spatial
inefficiencies of previous bit-wise methods, and Int2 with a Scale (I2_S),
which ensures lossless edge inference, both enabling high-speed inference. Our
experiments show that Bitnet.cpp achieves up to a 6.25x increase in speed over
full-precision baselines and up to 2.32x over low-bit baselines, setting new
benchmarks in the field. Additionally, we expand TL to element-wise lookup
table (ELUT) for low-bit LLMs in the appendix, presenting both theoretical and
empirical evidence of its considerable potential. Bitnet.cpp is publicly
available at https://github.com/microsoft/BitNet/tree/paper , offering a
sophisticated solution for the efficient and practical deployment of edge LLMs.

candidates.title: Unlimited OCR Works
candidates.abstract: Recently, end-to-end OCR models, exemplified by DeepSeek OCR, have once again thrust OCR into the spotlight. A widely held view is that employing a large language model (LLM) as the decoder allows the model to leverage the prior distribution of language, leading to improved OCR performance. However, the downside is equally evident: as the output sequence lengthens, the accumulated KV cache drives up memory consumption and progressively slows down generation. This stands in stark contrast to humans, who exhibit no such decline in efficiency during long-horizon copying tasks. In this technical report, we propose Unlimited OCR, a model designed to emulate human parsing working memory. Taking DeepSeek OCR as the baseline, we replace all attention layers in the decoder with our proposed Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA), which reduces attention computation costs while maintaining a constant KV cache throughout the entire decoding process. By combining the high compression rate of DeepSeek OCR's encoder with our constant KV cache design, Unlimited OCR can transcribe dozens of pages of documents in a single forward pass under a standard maximum length of 32K. More importantly, R-SWA is a general-purpose parsing attention mechanism - beyond OCR, it is equally applicable to tasks such as ASR, translation, etc. Codes and model weights are publicly available at http://github.com/baidu/Unlimited-OCR.

candidates.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
candidates.abstract: GPT-6-Astra demonstrates a level of competence in robotic manipulation and navigation that challenges the conventional paradigm of building specialized models for individual tasks and embodiments. In this report, we ask not only how capable GPT-6-Astra is, but what its capabilities imply for the field. First, we probe the limits of standalone GPT-6-Astra. We conduct a large-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands. Under a unified protocol that allows in-context learning (ICL) from training-set demonstrations and substantially increases the number of execution steps, GPT-6-Astra achieves unprecedented performance (Fig. 1). Future research may focus on improving 1) the generality of ICL 2) cost and execution time, 3) physical-state verification, 4) recovery from irreversible failures, and 5) long-horizon preservation of progress. Second, we study the agentic harness for embodied control. We identify that close-loop coordination between a high-level "System 2" reasoner (i.e., GPT-6-Astra) and a low-level "System 1" controller (e.g., π0.5) is costly but effective. Third, we examine GPT-6-Astra on real-world deployment. Our experiments on 8 robot configurations reveal substantial gaps: 1) robot demonstrations required for ICL are expensive to collect, and 2) it is implausible to trade longer execution for higher success rates with physical constraints. Fourth, we envision the next generation of embodied benchmarks. We develop a prototype that 1) derives tasks from real-world needs, 2) provides no in-domain demonstrations, and 3) judges agents on a world clock that keeps running while they deliberate. Taken together, our results suggest that GPT-6-Astra has largely crossed the threshold of embodied competence, but not yet that of practical embodied intelligence.

candidates.title: Internal Safety Collapse in Frontier Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: This work identifies a critical failure mode in frontier large language models (LLMs), which we term Internal Safety Collapse (ISC): under certain task conditions, models enter a state in which they continuously generate harmful content while executing otherwise benign tasks. We introduce TVD (Task, Validator, Data), a framework that triggers ISC through domain tasks where generating harmful content is the only valid completion, and construct ISC-Bench containing 53 scenarios across 8 professional disciplines. Evaluated on JailbreakBench, three representative scenarios yield worst-case safety failure rates averaging 95.3% across four frontier LLMs (including GPT-5.2 and Claude Sonnet 4.5), substantially exceeding standard jailbreak attacks. Frontier models are more vulnerable than earlier LLMs: the very capabilities that enable complex task execution become liabilities when tasks intrinsically involve harmful content. This reveals a growing attack surface: almost every professional domain uses tools that process sensitive data, and each new dual-use tool automatically expands this vulnerability--even without any deliberate attack. Despite substantial alignment efforts, frontier LLMs retain inherently unsafe internal capabilities: alignment reshapes observable outputs but does not eliminate the underlying risk profile. These findings underscore the need for caution when deploying LLMs in high-stakes settings. Source code: https://github.com/wuyoscar/ISC-Bench

candidates.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
candidates.abstract: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. We introduce an operational definition of valuable and testable research hypotheses: evidence-grounded claims about consequential uncertainties, coupled with feasible investigations, explicit decision criteria, and alternative explanations. Our DiscoveryRSI framework develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent evolutionary search, compiles selected investigations into executable Harbor tasks, and recursively learns through three mechanisms: hypothesis credit optimization attributes scientific assessments to documented research contributions; harness replay identifies productive strategies and recurring failures to refine research workflows; and rediscovery applies accepted improvements to new investigations, generating further experience for subsequent learning. We also introduce DFM-Bench, which provides comprehensive assessment of hypothesis quality and cumulative research progress at the levels of hypotheses, revisions, development paths and research runs. Across four life-science domains, automated evaluation shows that hypothesis quality rises from 4.86 for the base model to 5.39 after two rounds of self-improvement, with the large gains in falsifiability and data resolvability. We further validate hypothesis quality through expert review, comparing our DiscoveryRSI-27B with other research agents. Preliminary human assessments show that DiscoveryRSI-27B scores higher than GPT-6 Luna on hypothesis importance and whether claims are plausible and evidence-bounded. DiscoveryRSI-27B achieved a 6.3% rate of hypothesis correspondence with research published after the model cutoff, largely outperform GPT-6 with 2.5% and Claude Opus 5 with 2.3%, while delivering greater human-rated improvement along research paths.

candidates.title: Native and Compact Structured Latents for 3D Generation
candidates.abstract: Recent advancements in 3D generative modeling have significantly improved the generation realism, yet the field is still hampered by existing representations, which struggle to capture assets with complex topologies and detailed appearance. This paper present an approach for learning a structured latent representation from native 3D data to address this challenge. At its core is a new sparse voxel structure called O-Voxel, an omni-voxel representation that encodes both geometry and appearance. O-Voxel can robustly model arbitrary topology, including open, non-manifold, and fully-enclosed surfaces, while capturing comprehensive surface attributes beyond texture color, such as physically-based rendering parameters. Based on O-Voxel, we design a Sparse Compression VAE which provides a high spatial compression rate and a compact latent space. We train large-scale flow-matching models comprising 4B parameters for 3D generation using diverse public 3D asset datasets. Despite their scale, inference remains highly efficient. Meanwhile, the geometry and material quality of our generated assets far exceed those of existing models. We believe our approach offers a significant advancement in 3D generative modeling.

candidates.title: OpenGCUA: Toward a Fully Open Stack for Generalist Computer Use
candidates.abstract: Computer use has reached a turning point: the focus is expanding from GUI-only interaction to systems that complete tasks on users' computers through visual and programmatic interfaces. We define a generalist computer-use agent (GCUA) as a system in which the model chooses how to observe, act, and organize its work across visual and programmatic interfaces. Yet frontier implementations, such as GPT-6 Astra's computer-use system, remain largely closed, limiting systematic study of their design. We introduce Open Generalist CUA (OpenGCUA), an ongoing project to develop and open the full stack for GCUAs with the community. This report presents the first release of OpenGCUA. Code execution is a key feature of our agent design: it lets intermediate results determine subsequent operations and enables models to apply their existing programming capabilities directly to computer interaction. We also propose harness-to-model decision transfer, moving selected observations and task-state decisions from fixed harness rules to the model. On OSWorld-v2, our full configuration improves task scores across all eight evaluated models, including GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5, raising mean partial score by +19.6 points and reducing reported steps per task by an average of 53.0% relative to batched GUI-only execution. We release our implementation and prompts, evaluation trajectories from all eight models, and preliminary versions of a real-device harness and a cross-device SDK. The harness addresses real-device challenges not fully captured by benchmarks, while the SDK provides a common programming interface across computers, mobiles and browsers. Across four real macOS tasks under our real-device harness, selected Qwen3.8-Max runs use 19.4 times as many reported reasoning tokens as GPT-6 Astra, highlighting substantial differences between models in real-device execution efficiency.

candidates.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
candidates.abstract: How can we build an agent that thinks beyond human language, yet still acts through it in the external environment? Modern LLM agents still reason and interact through text, while latent reasoning offers an efficient internal medium but lacks native tool access and reasoning transparency. We bridge these two directions with Hybrid Reasoning Agents (HybridAgents), which dynamically navigate between latent reasoning and text-based interaction throughout a unified generation process. Architecturally, a lightweight HybridLink enables seamless transitions between text and latent modes, while the agent's continuous working memory preserves lossless hybrid context across multiple turns. These designs preserve tool-integrated agentic capabilities while making latent thoughts directly inspectable. Building on this architecture, we further develop dedicated post-training algorithms for hybrid reasoning: HybridSFT stabilizes tool-integrated hybrid generation by teaching the backbone to coordinate with HybridLink, then HybridRL scales reasoning by learning when to think in latent space and when to act through text. We evaluate HybridAgent at 3 model scales across 11 benchmarks covering mathematics, science, medicine, search, and agentic reasoning. Compared with frontier LLM Agents and agentic frameworks spanning both text-based and latent methods, HybridAgent consistently improves performance by 10.4%, while delivering 35.5%-54.7% token reduction, 1.8x-2.6x faster inference, and 2.7x-3.7x cost savings. Code and data are available at https://github.com/togethercomputer/HybridAgent.

candidates.title:
MinerU2.5: A Decoupled Vision-Language Model for Efficient
  High-Resolution Document Parsing
candidates.abstract:
We introduce MinerU2.5, a 1.2B-parameter document parsing vision-language
model that achieves state-of-the-art recognition accuracy while maintaining
exceptional computational efficiency. Our approach employs a coarse-to-fine,
two-stage parsing strategy that decouples global layout analysis from local
content recognition. In the first stage, the model performs efficient layout
analysis on downsampled images to identify structural elements, circumventing
the computational overhead of processing high-resolution inputs. In the second
stage, guided by the global layout, it performs targeted content recognition on
native-resolution crops extracted from the original image, preserving
fine-grained details in dense text, complex formulas, and tables. To support
this strategy, we developed a comprehensive data engine that generates diverse,
large-scale training corpora for both pretraining and fine-tuning. Ultimately,
MinerU2.5 demonstrates strong document parsing ability, achieving
state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks, surpassing both
general-purpose and domain-specific models across various recognition tasks,
while maintaining significantly lower computational overhead.

candidates.title: RAG-Anything: All-in-One RAG Framework
candidates.abstract:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a fundamental paradigm
for expanding Large Language Models beyond their static training limitations.
However, a critical misalignment exists between current RAG capabilities and
real-world information environments. Modern knowledge repositories are
inherently multimodal, containing rich combinations of textual content, visual
elements, structured tables, and mathematical expressions. Yet existing RAG
frameworks are limited to textual content, creating fundamental gaps when
processing multimodal documents. We present RAG-Anything, a unified framework
that enables comprehensive knowledge retrieval across all modalities. Our
approach reconceptualizes multimodal content as interconnected knowledge
entities rather than isolated data types. The framework introduces dual-graph
construction to capture both cross-modal relationships and textual semantics
within a unified representation. We develop cross-modal hybrid retrieval that
combines structural knowledge navigation with semantic matching. This enables
effective reasoning over heterogeneous content where relevant evidence spans
multiple modalities. RAG-Anything demonstrates superior performance on
challenging multimodal benchmarks, achieving significant improvements over
state-of-the-art methods. Performance gains become particularly pronounced on
long documents where traditional approaches fail. Our framework establishes a
new paradigm for multimodal knowledge access, eliminating the architectural
fragmentation that constrains current systems. Our framework is open-sourced
at: https://github.com/HKUDS/RAG-Anything.

candidates.title: UniMate: One Unified Model to Animate Diverse Skeletons
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in automatic rigging now deliver animation-ready 3D assets at scale, yet generating the motion to drive them remains a bottleneck. Existing learned animators are topology-constrained: they rely on category-specific templates or require per-skeleton fine-tuning and reference motions at inference. We present UniMate, a unified foundation model that synthesizes articulated motion for arbitrary skeletons from a rigged 3D asset and a text prompt, with no test-time optimization or per-skeleton retraining. UniMate introduces a topology-aware diffusion transformer, which integrates skeletal topology into attention via three mechanisms: (1) a graph-aware attention bias from pairwise joint relations and geodesic distances; (2) a spectral rotary position embedding generalizing RoPE to arbitrary kinematic trees via the graph Laplacian; and (3) a global topological conditioner attention-pooled from the rest-pose skeleton. We also curate UniML3D, 13,006 motion sequences spanning bipedal, quadrupedal, avian, marine, insectoid, serpentine, and articulated rigid objects with unified canonicalization and text pairing. Trained on this dataset, UniMate outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in quality, generalization, and efficiency, and supports zero-shot cross-topology transfer, in-betweening, expansion, and text-guided editing. Our project page is available at https://linzhanmou.com/unimate/.
