candidates.title: PS-CAHE: Protocol-Semantic and Confusion-Pair-Aware Fusion for UAV Intrusion Detection
candidates.abstract: Flow-based intrusion detection in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks can underuse protocol relationships and model complementarity. The Protocol-Semantic and Confusion-Pair-Aware Heterogeneous Ensemble (PS-CAHE) combines semantic features, training-only confusion-pair selection and two fusion weights. On 113,952 deduplicated UAVIDS-2025 flows, PS-CAHE achieved 95.58% Macro-F1 and 93.88% Matthews correlation coefficient on the fixed holdout. The full pipeline improved Macro-F1 by 0.83 percentage points over Original XGBoost; the pair-aware increment over global out-of-fold (OOF) weighting was only 0.15 points. Across 25 endpoint-pair-disjoint folds, this increment averaged 0.14 points (corrected 95% confidence interval: 0.06 to 0.22), positive in every fold. Three-base and matched two-base probability stacking scored higher in both nested protocols, with row-stratified advantages of 0.08 and 0.05 points. Strict no-port node-disjoint evaluation yielded 93.54% versus 93.78% for Original XGBoost; the corrected difference interval spanned zero, establishing no unseen-node advantage. Training-only temperature scaling reduced negative log-likelihood from 0.1097 to 0.1074 and expected calibration error from 0.88% to 0.49% without changing decisions. The small fusion increment has no demonstrated operational benefit. PS-CAHE offers directly inspectable, low-dimensional fusion on one simulator-generated benchmark; real-flight data, independent external datasets, temporal/mission shifts, open-set attacks and adversarial robustness remain unevaluated.

candidates.title: Explainable Sentiment-Based Reputational Risk Modelling in Ugandan Megaprojects
candidates.abstract: Reputational risk reflected in digital public discourse can significantly influence stakeholder perceptions, public trust, and decision-making surrounding government megaprojects. Existing computational approaches primarily focus on sentiment classification, offering limited capability for transparent and explainable modelling of reputational risk in public sector governance. This study proposes an explainable sentiment-informed model for identifying textual indicators of discourse-based reputational risk in digital discourse surrounding Ugandan government megaprojects. A corpus of 25,000 publicly available records from online news and social media sources was processed using a natural language processing pipeline, with weakly supervised labels subsequently validated through human validation of 2000 records by three independent annotators. A Soft Voting Ensemble integrating Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Logistic Regression, and Support Vector Machine classifiers was evaluated using stratified, independent human, and temporal validation. Under the primary stratified evaluation, the model achieved 96.0% accuracy, 0.9592 weighted F1, 0.9327 Macro-F1, and 0.9079 MCC. Independent human validation yielded 72.5% accuracy and 0.5952 Macro-F1, while temporal validation yielded 89.4% accuracy and 0.6108 Macro-F1. SHAP analysis of the Soft Voting Ensemble identified governance and project-related textual features contributing to model predictions. The findings demonstrate strong primary performance while also showing that performance is lower under independent human and temporal validation, supporting the use of the approach as an interpretable decision support framework for identifying discourse-based reputational risk signals rather than as a validated predictor of realized reputational outcomes.

candidates.title: Cost-Aware and Self-Validating Multi-Agent Engineering of Computer-Vision Pipelines: An Optimization-Based Framework with Applications to Remote-Sensing Image Analysis
candidates.abstract: Remote-sensing image analysis increasingly requires workflows that combine heterogeneous sensors, geospatial preprocessing, deep-learning models, uncertainty estimation, and domain-specific quality control. Conventional computer-vision pipelines are commonly designed manually, making them expensive to develop, difficult to reproduce, and inflexible when sensor quality or task requirements change. Recent agentic-AI systems have demonstrated the feasibility of automatically planning and executing computer-vision and AutoML workflows, but computational cost, geospatial validity, recovery behavior, and provenance remain insufficiently integrated. This paper proposes COSA-CV, a Cost-aware and Self-validating Agentic Computer-Vision framework for automated engineering of remote-sensing image-analysis pipelines. COSA-CV consists of specialized agents for task interpretation, dataset auditing, remote-sensing context analysis, pipeline planning, model and tool routing, image preprocessing, inference, post-processing, validation, error diagnosis, recovery, uncertainty estimation, cost monitoring, and report generation. Pipeline selection is formulated as a constrained multi-objective optimization problem that jointly considers predictive quality, processing latency, GPU usage, memory consumption, energy, tool-call cost, reliability, and human-review burden. The workflow is implemented as a stateful graph with conditional edges that dynamically select optical, SAR, or multimodal processing routes according to image quality, validation results, uncertainty, and computational budget. The evaluation includes two case studies: Sentinel-2 land-cover classification using EuroSAT and multimodal flood-region extraction using SEN12-FLOOD. The numerical results reported here are an illustrative worked example rather than measurements from real experiments, used only to demonstrate the framework&rsquo;s evaluation protocol and reporting format. In this hypothetical setting, COSA-CV is illustrated as reaching 94.7% accuracy and a 94.3% macro-F1 score for land-cover classification, and 85.2% Dice, 74.3% IoU, and 70.1% boundary F-score for flood-region extraction, with reduced computational cost and invalid-output acceptance relative to non-optimized multi-agent baselines. A final implementation must replace these illustrative values with results from real experiments before any of these comparative claims can be considered validated.

candidates.title: Two Timescales, Two Calibers: Auditing Consumer Adaptation in Algorithmically Mediated Environments
candidates.abstract: Platform analytics often use between-consumer behavioral differences to infer longitudinal consumer adaptation, although such differences need not describe changes within the same consumers. This study examines whether a matched between&ndash;within contrast retains its substantive interpretation across defensible analytical constructions. In algorithmically mediated environments, the study builds on established within&ndash;between decomposition and embeds a matched-estimand Caliber Divergence Index (CDI) in a portability audit spanning joint uncertainty, behavioral-opportunity conditioning, temporal conditioning, and behavioral representation. The primary analysis uses a longitudinal panel of 60,423 consumers (242,771 consumer-wave observations). In the focal matched-estimand specification, the between-consumer and within-consumer associations are both negative but differ in magnitude (&beta;B = &minus;2.9957, &beta;W = &minus;3.5132; CDI = 0.5174, BCa 95% CI [0.4757, 0.5573]). Opportunity conditioning reverses the contrast (CDI = &minus;0.4812), as does relative wave-position adjustment (&minus;0.8077). Continuous elapsed-time adjustment reduces it to approximately zero (&minus;0.0007), whereas integer-month fixed effects retain a positive contrast (+0.5186). Replacing top-brand share with brand HHI attenuates the contrast (+0.0565), with a confidence interval that includes zero. Competing generative regimes produce distinct signatures under the examined parameterizations, but none reproduces the focal empirical CDI. Complementary analyses of historical reviews and consumer-level behavior delineate temporal, measurement, and construct boundaries. Together, the findings show that a precisely estimated between&ndash;within contrast does not necessarily support a portable substantive interpretation across defensible analytical constructions.

candidates.title: Mobility and Logistics as a Service for Healthcare (MLaaS4H): Spatial Economic Models (SEMs) for Healthcare Facilities
candidates.abstract: The mobility of people and the transport of goods play an increasing role in the urbanization process. The Mobility as a Service (MaaS) paradigm represents an innovation for passenger mobility, while freight transport is evolving towards Logistics as a Service (LaaS). Hospitals act as major urban attractors, influencing both the travel patterns of workers and patients and the logistics flows associated with the distribution of goods and medicines. The hospital location generates significant territorial effects, impacting the spatial distribution of the population and economic activities. The combination of MaaS and LaaS for Healthcare generates the new acronym MLaaS4H (Mobility Logistics as a Service for Healthcare). This study analyzes these effects using consolidated Spatial Economic Models (SEMs), applied to a controlled benchmark system to evaluate the impacts of MaaS and the construction of a new hospital. The results show that changes in accessibility determine a modal shift from private transport to MaaS; the new hospital, with more employees, determines an increase in residents and employment; the land prices influence the spatial distribution of the population. These first findings can be replicated analytically using simple pen-and-paper computations and can be extended to the logistics component. They could offer useful support for land-use and transport planners, although parameter calibration and model validation against real-world case studies are still required.

candidates.title: Design Principles for Data-Centric Semantic Interoperability in IoT: The IoTTD Ontology
candidates.abstract: The increasing heterogeneity of Internet of Things (IoT) devices continues to challenge semantic interoperability across heterogeneous platforms and application domains. Although numerous IoT ontologies and standards have been proposed, many emphasize comprehensive semantic modeling, even in scenarios where only interoperable device data exchange is required, resulting in increased complexity, domain specificity, and limited adoption for generic device data exchange. This paper proposes a data-centric design approach for semantic interoperability based on a set of design principles specifically developed for the semantic representation of IoT device data. Guided by these principles, we introduce IoT Things&rsquo; Description (IoTTD), a lightweight OWL ontology that provides a standardized semantic representation for heterogeneous IoT device data. Rather than modeling the complete conceptual space of IoT systems, IoTTD focuses exclusively on the common semantic interface required for interoperable device data exchange. The ontology enables bidirectional semantic data sharing and supports generic SPARQL-based access without requiring prior knowledge of the IoTTD ontology&rsquo;s structure or content. IoTTD and the proposed design approach are evaluated through structural comparison with representative IoT ontologies, logical consistency verification using HermiT reasoning, semantic annotation examples, and representative application scenarios. The results demonstrate that IoTTD achieves substantially lower structural complexity while preserving the semantic capabilities required for interoperable IoT device data representation. The proposed design principles, together with their implementation in IoTTD, provide the foundation for lightweight semantic interoperability and can serve as a semantic basis for interoperable IoT Knowledge Graphs and Semantic Web applications.

candidates.title: Complementary Global&ndash;Local Feature Fusion and Ensemble Refinement for Facial-Expression Recognition on FER2013
candidates.abstract: Facial-expression recognition (FER) on FER2013 remains challenging because of low-resolution images, class imbalance, and label ambiguity. This study presents a global&ndash;local feature-fusion framework that integrates complementary representations with validation-based ensemble refinement. A frozen DINOv2 ViT-Base captures global facial semantics, while EfficientNetB3 extracts complementary local texture features. Their fused representation is used for seven-class facial-expression classification. The classification head is first trained with targeted feature-space SMOTE, and the EfficientNetB3 branch is then partially fine-tuned. Five-view test-time augmentation (TTA) is further incorporated at inference, together with an independently trained ConvNeXt-Tiny branch to provide additional architectural diversity. Ensemble weights are selected using a held-out validation set, while the test partition is reserved for final evaluation. On the 7178-image FER2013 test partition, the resulting ensemble achieves 76.51% accuracy, 75.77% macro F1, 76.32% weighted F1, 0.7158 Cohen&rsquo;s kappa, and 0.9574 macro ROC AUC. The results demonstrate the potential of combining complementary global&ndash;local representations, inference augmentation, and ensemble refinement for facial-expression recognition on FER2013.

candidates.title: Reactance-Aware Recursive Alignment for Human&ndash;AI Translation: Modeling Translator Agency and Task-Specific Critical Automation Capability
candidates.abstract: Professional translators may resist highly directive AI assistance when it threatens perceived autonomy, authorship, and control. This study introduces the Recursive Control and Alignment Protocol (ReCAP), a reactance-aware framework for interactive machine translation. ReCAP combines a reactance-potential model with a recursive loop of Intent Inference, Reactance-Guided Generation, and Critical Feedback Integration. Its Adversarial Reactance Minimization objective balances translation quality against estimated autonomy costs, and the task-specific Critical Automation Capability Index (CACI) provides an exploratory behavioral summary of critical engagement. In an evaluation with 156 professional translators across four English-based bidirectional language-pair settings, ReCAP achieved a mean COMET &times; 100 score of 36.8, 2.8 points above QE-guided MT (34.0), the strongest baseline, across five seed-matched runs per method&ndash;language-pair configuration. Mixed-effects estimates showed lower reported reactance for ReCAP than QE-guided MT (&beta; = &minus;0.55, 95% CI [&minus;0.71, &minus;0.39]) and higher exploratory CACI scores than CHORUS (&beta; = 0.64, 95% CI [0.44, 0.84]). Post hoc CACI checks remained task-specific and exploratory. These findings support a run-level translation-quality advantage and task-specific human-outcome associations under the evaluated conditions.

candidates.title: Personal Data Management System Architectures: A Systematic Review
candidates.abstract: The increase in personal data generation and the evolving landscape of digital information management necessitate robust and secure software architectures for personal data management systems. This systematic literature review examines the architectures proposed for such systems, classifying them as centralized, decentralized, or hybrid. The classification criterion is applied to the evidence the studies report rather than to the label its authors adopt. It separates the custody of the data from the coordination of its processing, because two systems that describe themselves as decentralized distribute only the former. The review analyzes 15 studies, retrieved from three databases, one search engine, and other sources, published between January 2014 and February 2026, examining the methodologies, technologies, and architectural strategies employed in personal data management systems. The review highlights the strengths and limitations of different software architectures in terms of scalability, security, and compliance with the European Union&rsquo;s General Data Protection Regulation, a regulatory regime addressed explicitly by several of the reviewed architecture studies. Key findings reveal a significant gap in the current literature. No shared benchmark or dataset appears in the corpus. The evidence therefore supports qualitative but not empirical comparison between architectural approaches.

candidates.title: A Lightweight Fine-Grained Malicious Request Detection Model Towards Smart Grid Cloud Services
candidates.abstract: To address the challenges in malicious request detection in smart grid cloud service scenarios, including the difficulty of effectively capturing the semantic relationships within payloads, the large parameter scale and high inference costs of pre-trained language models, an efficient and relatively lightweight, fine-grained malicious request detection model named DFEF-Net (DistilBERT-based FiLM-enhanced Expert Feature Network, DFEF-Net) is proposed. First, the model is based on the lightweight pre-trained language model DistilBERT and constructs 14-dimensional expert-based features to characterize the statistical information of request payloads, so as to strengthen its ability to represent request structural features and anomalous patterns. Second, the feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM) mechanism is introduced to adaptively modulate deep semantic features, effectively fusing semantic features with structural features. Finally, experiments on the proposed scheme are conducted on four public Web/HTTP attack datasets (HttpParams, HTTP CSIC 2010, FWAF, and SecureAI-SE). On these benchmarks, DFEF-Net achieves over 99% accuracy in binary attack detection on all four datasets. In multi-class attack identification, DFEF-Net reaches 99.27% macro-F1 on HttpParams and 97.00% on SecureAI-SE. RoBERTa slightly surpasses it on SecureAI-SE but drops to 59.53% macro-F1 on HttpParams, whereas DFEF-Net maintains balanced recognition across both datasets. Per-class analysis and multi-seed results further show relatively consistent fine-grained recognition across attack categories. Compared with BERT-based baseline models, DFEF-Net reduces model parameter count by approximately 39%, model size by 39%, FLOPs by 50%, and per-request inference latency by approximately 40&ndash;60% under the evaluated protocol. Consequently, the proposed approach offers a favorable trade-off among detection performance, computational cost, and fine-grained attack identification on the evaluated public Web/HTTP benchmarks, providing an efficient algorithmic basis for future evaluation in smart grid cloud services, while domain-specific validation on real smart-grid traffic remains necessary.

candidates.title: Quantifying the Impact of Construction Vessel Interference on Port Operations: An Agent-Based Simulation and Regression Analysis Framework
candidates.abstract: Port infrastructure development increasingly brings construction vessels into conflict with commercial shipping, yet quantitative assessments of such interference remain scarce. This study proposes a framework to quantify the impact of construction vessel activities on port operational efficiency. Three categories of construction vessels&mdash;channel-crossing, channel-occupying, and berth-occupying&mdash;are identified and modelled using agent-based simulation in AnyLogic. A virtual berth concept is introduced to represent construction vessel resource occupation, and the model is calibrated using data from a case-study port. Simulation outputs across varying traffic demand and construction vessel configurations are analyzed through multiple regression to derive quantitative estimates of interference. The results show that the three categories impose distinctly different levels of impact. Channel-occupying vessels have the most substantial effect, equivalent to approximately 8&ndash;10 commercial vessels at half the baseline demand level and 30&ndash;33 at three times the baseline level. Berth-occupying vessels correspond to roughly 2&ndash;4 and 20&ndash;22 commercial vessels, respectively, while channel-crossing vessels correspond to approximately 1.5&ndash;2.5 and 19&ndash;22. The framework is transferable to other port settings and provides a quantitative basis for prioritizing mitigation measures and informing construction scheduling.

candidates.title: DigiHerit: Enhancing Cultural Heritage Education Through Gamified Mobile Exploration
candidates.abstract: Digital technologies can provide alternative forms of access to cultural heritage sites that are physically restricted or unavailable to the public; however, their effective transformation into meaningful educational experiences requires the coordination of documentation, spatial representation, interpretation, interaction, and engagement. This study presents DigiHerit, a mobile gamified application developed for the digitally reconstructed Lassani Mansion in Kozani, Greece, and uses its implementation as the empirical basis for proposing a case-derived methodological framework for access-restricted architectural heritage. The implemented workflow combined spatial documentation, three-dimensional reconstruction and optimization, real-time application development, educational content integration, gamification, and user evaluation. Through retrospective analysis of the development process, seven interconnected methodological stages were identified, with Spatial Interpretation introduced as an explicit link between documentation and subsequent reconstruction and experience-design decisions. User evaluation with 30 participants suggests positive perceptions of digital access, engagement, learning, and exploration, while also identifying areas for improvement in navigation and content delivery. The study demonstrates how a case-specific technical workflow can inform a broader design methodology without prescribing particular technologies. The resulting framework is proposed as a case-derived structure for further prospective testing and refinement across different access-restricted heritage contexts and emerging modes of digital experience.

candidates.title: A Pose Landmark-Based Lightweight Human Fall-Detection Framework Using Spatiotemporal Features
candidates.abstract: In today&rsquo;s society, with its rapidly growing aging population, automated lightweight human fall detection has become very important. We present a lightweight human fall-detection framework based on pose landmarks and dynamic spatiotemporal motion features. The proposed system integrates YOLO12n and MediaPipe to detect human regions and extract pose landmarks from video sequences. The system incorporates a traceability information panel that visualizes the effects of different features on the classification of a frame as either a fall or an Activity of Daily Living (ADL) event. We introduce four override conditions, namely Head Position Override, Aspect Ratio Override, Vertical Leg Override, and Leg Alignment Override, to suppress false positives caused by ADL events such as bending, sleeping, picking up objects from the ground, and performing exercises. In addition, we utilize seven criteria, namely body angle, vertical drop, height ratio, angle change, knee-ankle vertical distance, vertical velocity, and head proximity to the ground, to distinguish fall events from ADL events effectively. We perform temporal validation of a fall event by confirming at least two consecutive fall frames to further reduce false positives. To evaluate the proposed method, we used two datasets, namely GMDCSA-24 and URFD. The proposed system achieved accuracy values of 90.63% and 88.57% on the GMDCSA-24 and URFD datasets, respectively.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence for Verification and Validation of Safety-Critical Systems: A Bibliometric Science-Mapping Study and an Assurance-Level Framework (AVAF) (2016&ndash;2026)
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and formal verification and validation (V&amp;V) are two of the most consequential areas in safety-critical systems engineering, and they interact in a dual way: AI is increasingly used to support V&amp;V, while V&amp;V is increasingly applied to certify AI components whose high-dimensional and emergent behaviors resist classical methods. This study provides one of the first comprehensive bibliometric and science-mapping analyses of AI-assisted V&amp;V for safety-critical systems over 2016&ndash;2026, combining, for the first time, Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection into a single PRISMA 2020-compliant corpus of 425 documents. Descriptive bibliometrics, keyword co-occurrence and thematic mapping, trend-topic detection, and logistic lifecycle modelling reveal a field growing at 21.8% annually, mobilizing 1249 authors across 54 countries and organized into four thematic communities, formal verification with machine learning, model checking with agentic AI and large language models, and AI-driven runtime monitoring of cyber-physical systems, with large language models, theorem proving, and AI-systems verification as the youngest themes. Findings are situated against emerging AI-governance regimes, including the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, the United States NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and ISO/IEC 42001. Beyond mapping, the study contributes the AI-Verification Assurance Framework (AVAF), a three-layer instrument that codes each study by verification direction, method, and property, grades the assurance it demonstrates on an A0&ndash;A4 scale, and maps it to certification regimes; AVAF is calibrated and pilot-tested on a stratified, subsample (intra-coder test&ndash;retest Cohen&rsquo;s &kappa; = 0.84). candidates.title: Multi-Channel Neighborhood-Constrained Variational Mode Decomposition
candidates.abstract: In many multi-channel engineering problems, the information relevant to the task is concentrated in one channel, while the other information plays an auxiliary role. In forecasting, the quantity to be predicted is the primary source of information and the covariates support it; in image processing, the image itself is primary and contextual data are auxiliary. This paper introduces multi-channel neighborhood-constrained variational mode decomposition (NCVMD), an extension of variational mode decomposition (VMD) built on this hierarchy. Where multivariate VMD (MVMD) aligns the modes&rsquo; central frequencies symmetrically and exactly across all channels, NCVMD distinguishes a main channel from auxiliary ones and makes the degree of alignment tunable, reallocating the decomposition error away from the priority channel by a controllable amount. A second contribution is a formal analysis of the resulting optimization problem, which delimits what can be asserted and what cannot. Every subproblem of the alternating scheme is convex and admits a unique closed-form solution, and the main channel provably attains the unconstrained VMD optimum, which MVMD cannot. The joint problem, however, remains nonconvex, so global optimality is not guaranteed. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data confirm the predicted behaviour.

candidates.title: Multi-Objective Security-Aware Workflow Scheduling with Soft Deadlines in Hybrid Clouds
candidates.abstract: Hybrid clouds allow service providers to combine secure private resources with elastic public resources, but most schedulers still have three practical limitations: they commonly model task security as a binary constraint, focus on independent tasks rather than dependent workflows, and treat deadlines as hard feasibility constraints rather than service-level objectives with economic penalties. MSWSS first ranks workflow tasks by deadline pressure, upward rank, security level, and penalty sensitivity; it then filters resources by security clearance; it next selects resources using a profit-aware multi-objective score; and finally it performs local migration and compaction to reduce execution cost and deadline loss. candidates.title: An AI-Augmented Decision Architecture for IT Investment: Linking Technical Maturity, Financial Valuation, and Accountable Governance
candidates.abstract: Open innovation makes IT investment decisions dependent on knowledge, technologies, and evidence that cross organizational boundaries. Yet these decisions are evaluated through disconnected logics: technical teams assess maturity; executives evaluate cost, strategic value, and flexibility; and artificial intelligence (AI) systems extract evidence or rank alternatives. Their separation creates a translation problem: maturity judgments enter financial models as unexamined assumptions, estimates remain detached from changing technical evidence, and algorithmic recommendations become difficult to contest. Its design is grounded in a secondary conceptual synthesis of a 39-study core drawn from three previously assembled evidence streams and two post-search updates published in 2026; it is neither a new systematic review nor an empirical validation. AIDA treats evidence bundles, readiness-risk profiles, value-option sets, decision cases, commitment packages, and outcome records as boundary objects coordinating internal and external actors. Twelve propositions specify expected relationships among traceability, uncertainty propagation, option-aware staging, explanation, role separation, feedback, and decision outcomes. The article also contributes a reusable constructed benchmark model: a generative-AI investment case, a fully parameterized 100,000-iteration Monte Carlo implementation, reproducibility files, and a comparative protocol that researchers can reuse, challenge, or extend to evaluate AIDA and alternative approaches. The benchmark demonstrates internal analytical behavior under declared assumptions rather than organizational superiority, while explicit escalation rules distinguish full AIDA from AIDA-Lite. Decision quality is expected to arise not from a single superior method, but from disciplined translation among distributed evidence, economic consequences, and accountable strategic judgment, particularly in open innovation ecosystems where evidence, incentives, and complementary assets span organizational boundaries.

candidates.title: Resource-Aware Strategic Planning for Partially Observable Star-Sector Tactical Games

candidates.title: On the Complexity of Encoded Nominal Data
candidates.abstract: Categorical data is a fundamental element of real-world tabular classification problems. In typical machine learning workflows, encoding strategies are used to convert categorical data into numerical representations. candidates.title: Source Intensity Errors and Data Correction Schemes in Downstream Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution Access Networks
candidates.abstract: Downstream multi-user continuous variable quantum key distribution (CV&ndash;QKD) based on passive optical networks represents a promising solution for large-scale quantum-secure access. However, global source errors can introduce biased parameter estimation and potential security vulnerabilities. To address this issue without additional hardware overhead, two data postprocessing correction schemes adapted to different deployment conditions are proposed. For scenarios with known intensity fluctuation statistics, a low-intensity pulse data tagging strategy is employed to construct conservative security bounds. For the more general scenario where only measurable intensity bounds are available, a worst-case bound-based parameter estimation framework is developed. The finite-size performance is further evaluated. Numerical results demonstrate that both schemes effectively eliminate security risks induced by intensity errors, maintain favorable multi-user scalability and acceptable finite-size performance, and provide a low-cost technical approach for the practical deployment of multi-user CV&ndash;QKD access networks.

candidates.abstract: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems have become a widely adopted management technology, even among small enterprises, driven by the expansion of cloud-based solutions that reduce infrastructure barriers. Although the literature has extensively examined critical success factors during implementation, the role of IT support as a permanent function sustaining system continuance and software evolution has received less attention. After applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, 45 studies published between 2020 and 2025 were selected and classified into five thematic categories: post-implementation critical success factors (38%), operational continuity and organizational performance (25%), incident management and technical support (13%), cloud ERP adoption (13%), and user training and change management (11%). Results show that IT support is a cross-cutting factor determining post-deployment lifecycle resilience, ERP stability, and availability, whose effectiveness depends on top management backing and organizational structure. Beyond synthesizing existing critical success factors, this study proposes an IT support maturity model, comprising Reactive, Formalized, and Preventive/Analytical levels, that offers small enterprises a diagnostic instrument to assess their current support architecture and identify concrete pathways toward more resilient ERP post-deployment lifecycle dynamics.

candidates.title: An Uncertainty-Aware Decision-Support System for Composite-Property Prediction with Physically Admissible Conformal Intervals
candidates.abstract: Machine-learning surrogates predict composite properties but report no calibrated reliability and may violate physics. Bound-constrained conformal prediction confines intervals to physical bounds but assumes them exact. This paper keeps the corridor as a hard constraint and characterizes what a decision-support system guarantees when it is wrong. If a fraction &eta; of responses lies outside the corridor, no admissible interval covers more than 1&minus;&eta;, so the nominal level 1&minus;&alpha; is attainable only if &eta;&le;&alpha;. A projection-aware calibration scores out-of-corridor points as infinitely nonconforming. Its marginal coverage is at least 1&minus;&alpha;&minus;&eta;&pi;&infin; at every calibration size (&pi;&infin; the fallback probability); its coverage across calibrations follows an exact Beta law. In the limit it reaches the nominal level whenever attainable; calibrate-then-clip loses up to &eta;. For &eta;&lt;&alpha; the system thus delivers admissible intervals at the nominal level for a small, quantified width premium, with a feasibility verdict and a Shapley explanation. Across eight datasets it recovers the nominal level on a woven laminate with a misspecified rule-of-mixtures bound (90.3% against 85.6% for naive projection) and tracks the frontier under normative bounds the data contradict. Under exact Voigt&ndash;Reuss bounds it removes all violations and narrows intervals thirteen-fold. Width, paid inside the corridor, is the price.

candidates.title: Capability, ranking dynamics, and inference pricing in the large language model ecosystem: evidence from linked public data
candidates.abstract: Public leaderboards and pricing catalogues offer complementary but hard-to-combine views of the large language model ecosystem. We analyse three linked public sources: an archived Open LLM Leaderboard v2 sample of 4,565 open-weight evaluation records with complete six-benchmark scores; an 89-snapshot human-preference panel of 279 models (June 2024–August 2025); and 2,685 priced chat endpoints (October 2026). Principal component analysis identifies a dominant common component (74% of benchmark variance), retained by parallel analysis and robust to family deduplication. Benchmark performance rises with parameter count (13.6 points per tenfold) and with submission date at constant size and type (10.5 points per year) under family-clustered inference. A documented change of the default rating on 20 May 2025 shifted all listed scores by about 18 points; within the stable period the preference frontier rose by about 187 points per year relative to a fixed reference set through 17 leaders with median spells of 12 days, top-20 slots concentrated among fewer organisations, and ratings did not drift within models. Among 201 models listed by three or more providers, the median maximum-to-minimum price ratio is 1.38 (1.27 under version-strict identifiers). A hedonic model adjusting for time since first listing attributes multipliers of about 3.1 to one standard deviation of arena score and 0.18 to open-weight status, robust to version-exact matching. Preference ratings and benchmark averages agree strongly for 69 matched models. Temporal mismatch, selective coverage, and related model families preclude causal interpretation.

candidates.title: OBLIVION TextLM: A Query-relative Control Plane for Efficient Generative Language-model Inference
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Long-context language models can ingest far more information than a particular query actually requires, yet retaining every represented distinction is neither equivalent to using it well nor automatically computationally efficient. We present OBLIVION TextLM, a model-agnostic query-relative control plane that operationalizes unresolved semantic obligations around a separately licensed pretrained language-model executor. The system constructs a live obligation state, routes evidence against that state, invokes the executor, permits new obligations to be born from intermediate evidence, generates evidence-bound completion certificates, verifies discharge conservatively, and retires an obligation only when verification and an explicit net-gain audit both succeed. Three matched modes—full-context baseline, retrieval-augmented generation, and OBLIVION—use the same executor to separate foundation-model quality from retrieval and control effects. The v2.0.0 reference implementation adds hybrid routing, citations, memory, streaming OpenAI-compatible clients, verifier separation, tracing, usage accounting, benchmarking, safety utilities, and advisory KV-cache ownership hooks. We validate the artifact by compilation, 29 automated tests, release-metadata checks, and deterministic three-mode smoke runs. We deliberately distinguish text-level semantic retirement from unmeasured physical KV-cache or GPU savings. The contribution is an executable, falsifiable systems framework for testing when verified query-relative state control improves quality–compute trade-offs without claiming a separately trained foundation model of its own.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Enabling Efficient Serverless Inference Serving for LLM (Large Language Model) in the Cloud
candidates.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">This review report examines the problem of cold-start latency in serverless inference for large language models (LLMs) and surveys recent systems that address it, with a particular focus on ServerlessLLM. In serverless environments, loading multi-hundred-gigabyte LLM checkpoints and initializing GPU resources can dominate end-to-end latency, making real-time applications such as conversational agents and translation services difficult to deploy cost-efficiently. The report first summarizes the cold-start problem and common mitigation strategies in today's Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) platforms, including container warming, host-side checkpoint caching, and cluster-level storage servers. It then reviews the design of ServerlessLLM, which exploits underutilized multi-tier storage in GPU servers, a loading-optimized checkpoint format, live inference migration based on token-level state transfer, and a startup-time-aware model scheduler. Additional methods from recent literature, such as RainbowCake's layered container caching, and the cold-start handling mechanisms of major cloud providers are also discussed. Drawing on the evaluation presented in the original work, the report highlights that multi-tier checkpoint loading and live migration reduce model startup time by up to 6-8× compared to conventional formats, and deliver up to 28× lower startup latency than Ray Serve for large models in realistic traces. The review concludes by outlining open challenges and future directions, including integrating model compression, multi-level inference pipelines, and advanced memory-offloading techniques to further improve the scalability and efficiency of serverless LLM inference.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Hallucination Mitigation in Large Language Models: A Review and Exploratory Small-Model Pilot
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Large language models (LLMs) can produce fluent responses that are false, unsupported, outdated, or more certain than the available evidence justifies. This manuscript presents a narrative review of major hallucination-mitigation approaches and an exploratory pilot intended to refine a future evaluation protocol rather than establish model-level performance. The review covers false-premise handling, abstention and knowledge-boundary estimation, retrieval-augmented generation, grounding, verification, self-checking, and multimodal hallucination. It also distinguishes published evidence from an engineering proposal for failure-driven correction. The pilot used a locally executed interface labeled Gemma 3 1B-IT and ten hand-designed stress prompts spanning false premises, insufficient evidence, fabricated-citation traps, unknowable events, and future-value requests. The revised analysis deliberately avoids compressing these observations into a single hallucination score. Two responses were epistemically appropriate, three were partially appropriate but introduced unsupported content, and five failed the target behavior. Generation stability was tracked separately: one otherwise appropriate answer entered a repetition loop, and another item required a restart after a context-length error. An extended follow-up run was terminated when the local system became unstable and began returning empty outputs; those observations are reported only qualitatively. The pilot is too small and insufficiently controlled to support causal claims or generalization to the Gemma family. Its value is methodological: it illustrates why hallucination research should report multiple axes - factual correctness, false-premise resistance, correct abstention, unnecessary abstention, grounding fidelity, coverage, calibration where available, and generation stability - rather than one aggregate number. The literature further suggests that mitigation is most credible when model behavior, external evidence, verification, and evaluation design are treated as a coupled system.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Prompt-Shape- and Prefix-Cache-Aware CPU/NPU Routing for Large Language Model Inference on Edge SoCs
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Large language model (LLM) inference on edge systems must exploit heterogeneous central processing unit (CPU) and neural processing unit (NPU) resources under tight memory and latency constraints. Because prefilling and autoregressive decoding have different computational characteristics, the fastest backend depends on the request shape and prefix-cache reuse. This work proposes request-level CPU/NPU routing for the RK3588 system on chip (SoC). Prompt-shape-aware routing (PSR) uses prompt length and generation budget to select a backend for no-cache requests, while prefix-cache-aware routing (PCAR) additionally models reusable-prefix length, remaining prefill workload, full-context effects, and cache-path state with backend-specific latency models. On 49 no-cache held-out workloads, PSR achieves 97.96% backend-selection accuracy and a relative oracle loss of 0.121% ± 0.010%. On 45 independent cache-aware held-out workloads, accounting for the remaining prefill workload reduces relative oracle loss from 4.926% ± 0.378% for PSR(raw) to 0.425% ± 0.060% for PSR(eff). The complete PCAR model further reduces it to 0.205% ± 0.043%, improves selection accuracy from 93.33% to 95.56%, and provides an additional 0.22% cumulative-latency reduction over that of PSR(eff). These results show that jointly modeling request shape and prefix-cache state enables near-oracle heterogeneous LLM inference routing on edge SoCs.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Beyond Disclosure: Reframing Privacy as Inference Impedance in Large Language Models
candidates.abstract:
<jats:p>Contemporary debates in AI ethics continue to frame privacy primarily in terms of disclosure, identifiability, and data access.
This article argues that such a framing is no longer sufficient for embedding-based artificial intelligence systems. We introduce
the Deep Personal Privacy (DPP) framework, which reconceptualizes privacy as inference impedance within high-dimensional
semantic representation spaces. Rather than asking whether information has been revealed, DPP evaluates how easily sensitive
attributes can be inferred from latent embeddings. We model embedding spaces as semantic transmission layers that enable
indirect attribute inference through geometric alignment. Privacy risk is therefore defined in terms of cosine similarity, inference
probability, and logarithmic impedance within structured inference graphs. The framework integrates ontology-driven
sensitive expression mapping, representation-level perturbation mechanisms, and a multi-objective optimization procedure
balancing utility and privacy. mpirical demonstrations show that DPP-based interventions reduce semantic alignment with
sensitive concept prototypes and increase inference resistance while maintaining acceptable task erformance. Conceptually,
the framework advances a paradigm shift in AI ethics: privacy must be evaluated not only by what systems disclose, but by what
they are capable of inferring. DPP thus complements existing structural and statistical privacy approaches by introducing a
representation-level metric for inferential power asymmetry</jats:p>

                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are processed from structured precursors and subsequently loaded into Argonaute proteins to repress target mRNAs. Accurate decoding of mature miRNAs from precursor sequences is fundamental to miRNA annotation and the rational engineering of artificial miRNAs. However, existing computational approaches are largely developed for humans, with limited ability to generalize across diverse plants, animals, and viruses. Moreover, a unified data-driven framework that links mature-miRNA decoding with the predictive design of artificial miRNA precursors is still lacking, restricting the scalable application of miRNA biotechnology across species.</jats:p>

                  <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We develop and evaluate miRstring, a biogenesis-aware RNA language framework for decoding the four boundaries of mature miRNAs from precursor context across species, and further investigate its utility for cross-species miRNA annotation and rational artificial miRNA design.</jats:p>

                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>miRstring, a biogenesis-aware RNA language framework, was developed using 77,708 miRNA precursors spanning 414 species. The model was evaluated against existing methods under both family-held-out and species-held-out settings to assess its ability to generalize to unseen miRNA families and species. Attention-based analyses were further performed to examine whether miRstring captured biologically relevant features associated with miRNA processing, and the framework was subsequently applied to predictive design of artificial miRNA precursors.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Weak Distributive Inference in Language Acquisition
candidates.abstract: We find that children compute distributive inferences, and thus that they are capable pragmatic reasoners when alternatives can be derived without lexical substitution. This provides further evidence that they are not limited by other factors like working memory or pragmatic tolerance. In addition, we find evidence that children consistently computed weak distributive inferences. In the spirit of Fox’s (2007) grammatical account, such inferences require double application of Exh, one scoping above the universal quantifier and another below. Thus, not only do children compute implicatures, but they appear to adopt the more complex parse—embedding one operator inside another—rather than relying on the simpler, global option that generates a strong distributive inference.

candidates.title: Fall-Related Safety Hazard Analysis in Construction Using Vision-Language Models and Natural Language Inference
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Fall accidents account for more than one-third of fatalities in construction, and fall-related hazards introduce a significant risk of occupational injuries to construction workers. Although numerous efforts have been devoted to preventing falls, most studies have focused on detecting predefined hazards, with less consideration of understanding the context in which hazardous conditions arise. Most previous studies are limited in identifying combined hazardous conditions, consisting of multiple safety violations, such as a missing safety lanyard on an unprotected open edge on a scaffold. In this context, this study proposes an integrated fall hazard analysis framework using a vision-language model that converts visual information into hazard-descriptions aligned with legal safety standards. Then, the framework analyzes the hazard-related texts using natural language inference to recognize the risk of hazards. By leveraging the BLIP-2 architecture, the proposed method establishes independent image captioning models for three critical categories directly associated with fall accidents: openings, scaffolding, and worker behavior. The framework classifies images as “Safe” or “Risk” based on generated descriptions that strictly adhere to occupational safety and health standards. The proposed fall-hazard assessment framework achieves an F1-score of 0.84, indicating its significant practical potential for comprehensive fall hazard analysis in real-world construction environments.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Inference Without Stakes: What Large Language Models Do-and Do Not-Show About Intelligence
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Large language models have made a powerful case for the reach of statistical inference. They produce fluent language, solve heterogeneous problems, and exhibit forms of abstraction that cannot be dismissed as simple retrieval. Their success, however, does not establish that inference is sufficient for intelligence. That conclusion follows only by sliding between distinct ideas: inferential competence, task performance, agency, and phenomenal awareness. This essay separates them. It argues that inference is always organized by a prior structure of relevance-a specification of which distinctions, errors, goals, and outcomes matter. In biological agents, that relevance is continually shaped through self-maintenance, embodied action, developmental history, and exposure to the consequences of action. Present language models largely inherit it from humangenerated corpora, training objectives, prompts, evaluation procedures, and deployment institutions. They therefore possess what I call borrowed worldliness: genuine competence acquired from the traces of human engagement with the world, without yet displaying the autonomous normative organization characteristic of ecological agency. Drawing on active inference, ecological psychology, Umwelt theory, and enactivism, the essay develops a substrate-neutral account of this distinction. The argument neither denies the capacities of language models nor rules out artificial agency. It establishes a narrower conclusion: successful inference, even when remarkably general, is not by itself sufficient evidence of an agent for whom anything is at stake.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Asymptotic Equivalence of the Switching Degree with Unknown Boundary — √n-Inference Adaptivity in the Fixed-Breakpoint Model, Finite-Sample Correction Directions, and a Post-Selection Inference Framework

<jats:p><p><span>The two-step estimation procedure in structural break detection gives rise to a post-selection inference problem: when the regime boundary is unknown and is first estimated by a test statistic, and the switching degree is then computed on either side of the estimated boundary, the plug-in estimator Ŝ_plug differs from the estimator Ŝ_known obtained with a known boundary. In this paper we prove, in the fixed-breakpoint model (where the switching difference vector Δθ is fixed and nonzero), a core theoretical result: the asymptotic equivalence theorem. Under assumptions A1–A7,</span></p>
<p><span>√n (Ŝ_plug − Ŝ_known) = o_p(1),</span></p>
<p><span>and hence</span></p>
<p><span>√n (Ŝ_plug − S) →_d N(0, V₀),</span></p>
<p><span>exactly as in the known-boundary case. The source of this result is the n-consistency of the boundary estimator in the fixed-breakpoint model: the number of misclassified samples is O_p(1), their effect on the estimated coefficients is O_p(n⁻¹), and this is invisible at the √n scale. Building on this result, we discuss finite-sample correction directions: (i) a first-order heuristic expansion of the conditional bias, indicating that the post-selection bias, although invisible at the √n scale, may be relevant in finite samples; (ii) a fixed-design residual bootstrap scheme, proposed as a working hypothesis, which keeps the design points (Tᵢ, Xᵢ) fixed and resamples only residuals, aiming to mimic the uncertainty of the boundary selection process; (iii) asymmetric bootstrap quantile confidence intervals as a construction proposal. We strictly distinguish proved theorems from unproved working hypotheses. The paper is purely theoretical; numerical validation is an open problem.</span></p>

candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Natural Language Inference (NLI) deals with the problem of logical entailment between two sentences. It is evidenced that apart from interpretation of words and syntactic structures, use of external relevant knowledge is also required. This paper investigates whether the integration of external knowledge, represented as triplets and extracted from Knowledge Graphs (KGs), can improve the performance of a pretrained language model on NLI tasks. It also investigates how the source of knowledge affects performance. Six benchmark datasets, namely RTE, QNLI, SICK, SNLI, DNLI, and SciTail, were enriched with knowledge extracted from AristoTuple and WordNet, while ConceptNet was additionally used for the SNLI and SciTail datasets. Enrichment was applied only to the training data through a strict relevance-based selection mechanism using paraphrase-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings and cosine-similarity filtering, and the resulting datasets were used to fine-tune BERT-base-uncased. Evaluation included method-specific configurations selected through validation-based hyperparameter exploration and a controlled multi-seed setting using the vanilla baseline hyperparameters with matched seeds across baseline and enriched datasets. The best observed validation accuracy was 95.24% on SciTail with AristoTuple, while the highest test accuracy, also on SciTail, was 93.70% with ConceptNet. Across both evaluation settings, the effect of knowledge enrichment varied across datasets and knowledge sources, with the multi-seed analysis further assessing the robustness of these effects under controlled training conditions. Overall, the proposed data-level approach achieved competitive performance compared with more complex knowledge-enhanced NLI methods. A taxonomy of existing NLI approaches is also presented.</jats:p>

candidates.title: CTC score-based transcription quality annotation for stable text-to-speech synthesis training on noisy transcriptions
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Automatic speech recognition (ASR) has been increasingly adopted for generating transcriptions to train text-to-speech (TTS) models, substantially reducing manual annotation costs. However, transcription errors introduced by ASR systems inevitably degrade TTS performance, and existing approaches lack explicit quality awareness, leaving it unclear whether TTS models can learn to distinguish and respond to varying transcription quality. This study investigates whether explicit quality supervision can enable TTS models to develop quality-aware representations and achieve controllable stable synthesis. This study proposes transcription quality labels (TQL), automatically derived from connectionist temporal classification scores. During training, TQL provides explicit quality supervision, enabling the model to associate transcription quality with acoustic characteristics. During inference, setting TQL to high values guides the model toward stable synthesis that faithfully follows the input text. Under controlled conditions isolating the effect of transcription quality, our best TQL-based model achieves 8.4% word error rate compared to 15.9% for the baseline, a 47% relative reduction. While synthesis accuracy gains are significant, naturalness improvements are modest (mean opinion score of 3.66 vs. 3.55), indicating that TQL primarily enhances synthesis stability rather than perceptual quality. Further analysis confirms that synthesis quality varies systematically with TQL values at inference, demonstrating learned quality-conditioned behavior.</jats:p>

candidates.title: From Pixels to Pairs: A Comprehensive Benchmark of LLM-Driven Key–Value Extraction in Noisy Document Settings
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in document key–value pair(KVP) extraction, yet controlled evaluations of their robustness to optical character recognition (OCR)output remain limited. This leaves an important gap in understanding their reliability within real-world OCR-to-LLM pipelines. Unlike end-to-end Vision-Language Models (VLMs) that conflate visualperception with semantic extraction, modular pipelines allow errors to be explicitly isolated andaudited. To bridge this evaluation gap, we introduce a controlled, large-scale benchmarking frameworkdesigned to distinguish downstream LLM extraction behavior from upstream OCR degradation. Thisbenchmark evaluates 136 experimental configurations and 17,688 deterministic document-level inferenceinstances across five instruction-tuned open-weight LLMs (2B–8B parameters), three complementarydatasets, and four text-quality conditions. This extensive matrix pairs a full zero-shot comparisonand targeted one- to three-shot experiments with a confirmatory sensitivity analysis comprising 40configurations across 20 frozen demonstration sets. By separating Key Recall (annotated-field recovery)from Exact Match and Value F1 (exact and partial value recovery, respectively), we reveal whetherOCR degradation affects field identification and value reproduction differently across models. Crucially,our findings challenge three practical evaluation assumptions: (1) that clean-text performance is areliable proxy for real-world robustness, (2) that model rankings remain consistent across annotation-derived Gold and OCR-derived text conditions, and (3) that providing few-shot demonstrationsmonotonically improves extraction accuracy. By exposing vulnerabilities such as model-rankingreversals and unstable few-shot gains, this benchmark provides a rigorous and reproducible frameworkfor evaluating LLM reliability under noisy document conditions. To facilitate reproducible research,our entire benchmarking framework, dataset splits, and evaluation scripts are open-sourced.

candidates.title: Leverage and Structural Information in Noisy Stochastic-volatility Prices
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Leverage can preserve information about a hidden volatility drift as covariance shrinks, provided its response propagates through the latent dynamics. For a bivariate Ornstein–Uhlenbeck model observed through noisy log-price levels on a fixed grid, we prove exact identification at positive covariance and adaptive squared drift risk of order min{1, [n(s² + se²)]⁻¹}, where n counts observation blocks, s is the covariance scale and e the leverage amplitude. Matching lower bounds on specified drift neighborhoods use the full price law. Dynamically exciting leverage thus permits learning where zero leverage prevents uniform consistency. Nuisance parameters are unknown; confidence coverage includes zero covariance and absent excitation. Precision requires fixed excitation and residual covariance margins, fixed positive level noise, a nonaliased drift branch and a sufficiently small, unevaluated covariance ceiling.</jats:p>

candidates.title: From Noisy Prescription Images to Reliable Text-Line Localization: Preprocessing and Segmentation for Handwritten Medical OCR in South Sudan
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Handwritten prescription recognition in low-resource healthcare depends not only on the accuracy of the recognition network but also on the quality of the image presented to that network. This study implemented and evaluated a preprocessing and segmentation pipeline designed to convert noisy, variably illuminated and geometrically inconsistent prescription images into standardised inputs suitable for handwritten-text recognition. The workflow was grounded in a quantitative experimental design using the Doctor's Handwritten Prescription BD dataset, comprising 4,680 segmented pharmaceutical-word images and a 60%/20%/20% train-validation-test partition. The pipeline combined grayscale conversion, adaptive thresholding and binarization, Hough-transform-based skew correction, morphological denoising, aspect-ratio-preserving resizing and a final segmentation confirmation stage intended for line localization on unsegmented prescription pages. Segmentation performance was evaluated using Intersection over Union (IoU), with a pre-specified acceptance criterion of 0.90 or higher. The source dissertation states that segmentation success was confirmed at or above this threshold, but it does not separately tabulate an exact IoU point estimate; this article therefore reports the threshold-level result without inventing additional precision. The pipeline is technically important because each stage targets a distinct source of variance that can degrade downstream feature extraction: illumination, background noise, rotation, scale and boundary uncertainty. The study further incorporated contextual augmentation to reduce the mismatch between the Bangladesh-origin source corpus and the intended South Sudanese application environment. The results support the preprocessing and localization design as a necessary front end for the Residual U-Net recognition system, while also showing that external validity remains limited by the absence of a fully local prescription corpus. A clinically credible next step is prospective validation using authentic South Sudanese prescription images, with explicit reporting of IoU distributions, failure cases and computational cost on low-resource hardware.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Improving accuracy of differential parameter extraction from noisy measurement data
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>The paper addresses the problem of enhancing the accuracy of differential analysis of integral characteristics of semiconductor structures under conditions of experimental noise. It is shown that standard measurement methods with a linear voltage step lead to significant errors in calculating the dimensionless sensitivity, manifesting themselves as non-physical oscillations that complicate the identification of charge transport mechanisms. A comparative analysis of three data processing methods is conducted: the optimal step method, polynomial approximation (Savitzky–Golay filter), and adaptive filtering based on the Kalman algorithm. It is established that application of the optimal step method based on logarithmic current sampling avoids differentiation artifacts without introducing phase delays characteristic of smoothing methods. The proposed approaches are tested on experimental current-voltage characteristics of OLED structures, confirming their suitability for precise diagnostics of electrophysical parameters of semiconductor devices.</jats:p>

candidates.title: A Supervised Morphosyntactic Analyzer for Modern and Classical Arabic Text
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Arabic morphological analysis remains a central challenge for natural language processing (NLP). This challenge is embedded within the complex, rich, and multi-layered morphology of Arabic, where orthographic words encode enclitics, root-and-pattern derivations, and other morphosyntactic features. Another dimension of complexity is the coexistence of different varieties of Arabic, including Modern Standard Arabic (MSA), Classical Arabic (CA), and Dialectal Arabic (DA). In this four-phase empirical investigation of Arabic, a new, standardized CoNLL-U benchmark integrating the Arabella corpus (MSA) and the MASAQ corpus (CA) was evaluated across different settings. This paper aims to build a baseline morphological analyzer by evaluating a wider range of supervised systems, including lexicon-lookup, Conditional Random Fields (CRFs), full fine-tuning of Arabic PLMs, and AraT5 configurations. A parameter-efficient LoRA adaptation of QARiB was implemented, preserving most UPOS performance with minor differences. The results of the comparative evaluation of a variety of models across all settings were reported, and significant results were emphasized. The findings demonstrate severe limitations in current capabilities, particularly that cross-domain transfer for fine-grained language-specific tags (XPOS) remains difficult. Also, models struggle with the asymmetry of cross-register transfer, as moving from Classical to Modern Arabic exposes a lack of coverage for modern named entities and punctuation.</jats:p>

candidates.title: A Hilbert Transform N-Dimensional Noisy Phase Unwrapping Algorithm
candidates.abstract:
<jats:p>Phase  unwrapping  arises  as  a  key  step  in  several  imaging  technologies,  from  which  we 
emphasize  remote  sensing  applications  like  terrain  analysis  and  generation,  topographic  mapping, 
interferometric synthetic aperture radar (ISAR). Due to various decorrelation factors, there is much noise in 
phase images. Phase noise degrades the visual quality of images and interferograms, increases the errors of 
results  derived  from  the  ISAR  interferogram,  and  obstruct  phase  unwrapping.  Hilbert  transform  (HT)  as  a 
phase  unwrapping  techniques  was  recently  proposed,  and  its  behavior  in  presence  of  noise  is  unknown.  In 
this paper, one-dimensional (1-D) HT phase unwrapping algorithm is proposed to detect and eliminate phase 
discontinuities  in  N-dimensional  (N-D)  noisy  phase  arrays.  The  behavior  of  this  method  in  presence  of 
different noise levels is studied and compared with the other approach of phase jump detection. The phase 
noise  filtration  problem  and  its  effect  on  proposed  algorithm  behavior  are  considered.  Tests  of  method 
presented illustrate the validity and effectiveness of proposed algorithm for difficult problems with noisy and 
discontinuous original phases.</jats:p>

candidates.title: PERFORMANCE COMPARISON OF MODERN LOSSY COMPRESSION TECHNIQUES WITH APPLICATION TO GRAYSCALE NOISY IMAGES
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>The object of the study is the process of lossy compression of noisy grayscale images by modern coders based on discrete cosine transform using several quality metrics. The subject of the study is the method to determine parameters that control compression to provide the highest quality of compressed images or the best compression ratio for the considered type of images.The goal of the study is to analyze performance characteristics for test images of different complexity and produce recommendations concerning the coder selection and its parameters setting. Methods used: numerical simulation, verification for a set of test images. Results obtained: 1) optimal operation point exists in many cases where its existence is more probable for a larger noise intensity, simpler structure images, and more efficient coders; 2) the better portable graphics coder usually provides the best compromise between image quality and compression ratio; 3) a rather high correlation of performance characteristics of compression techniques based on discrete cosine transform is observed. Conclusions: 1) it is often possible to provide a rather large compression ratio without losing valuable information or even with improving the image quality; 2) performance characteristics of lossy compression considerably depends on image complexity and, thus, the parameter that controls compression has to be adapted to image and noise characteristics. </jats:p>

candidates.title: Error Signal Based Method for Real Time Pitch Extraction from Noisy Speech
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Pitch estimation efficiency always gets affected by two major phenomena. The first one is additive noise which by nature are not correlated with the source speech signal. The second one is the vocal tract effect which creates unnecessary peaks within the signal waveform, resulting inaccurate detection of the pitch value. This paper proposes a Modified Weighted Autocorrelation Function (MWAF) executed in the Linear Predictive Coding (LPC) residual domain, instead of directly executing over the noisy source speech signal. Converting the noisy source speech signal to LP residual helps eliminating the vocal tract effects and emphasizing the necessary effects of glottal excitation. The Autocorrelation Function (ACF) and the Circular Average Magnitude Difference Function (CAMDF) are directly applied on this residual. The proposed MWAF is then calculated by multiplying the ACF with the reciprocal of the CAMDF, which enhances the periodic components as well as reduces the noise induced false peaks. Experimental results were evaluated on the KEELE and NTT databases across White, Babble, Train and HF Channel noise conditions. The result shows that our proposed algorithm reduces the Gross Pitch Error (GPE) by an average of 40.34% compared to baseline methods such as BaNa, PEFAC and WAF. Furthermore, the algorithm achieves an overall computational gain of 53.44% compared to BaNa, PEFAC and WAF, offering a stable solution for pitch tracking in degraded acoustic conditions.</jats:p>

candidates.title: A Systematic Benchmark of Quantum Support Vector Machines for Interpretable Attribution of AI-Generated Text
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Reliable attribution of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated text to a specific large language model (LLM) matters increasingly as LLMs proliferate, yet where quantum machine learning actually stands on this task has, to our knowledge, never been measured systematically. We benchmark the quantum support vector machine (QSVM) for binary attribution between Gemma 3 and Qwen 2.5 on a 5800-sample corpus from paired prompts: 83 configurations sweeping qubit count, regularization, training-set size, feature-map family, and circuit depth under exact, noiseless classical statevector simulation. QSVM validation accuracy plateaus at approximately 88%, whereas a classical support vector machine with a radial basis function kernel reaches approximately 97.8% on the identical fourteen-dimensional inputs: the ceiling belongs to the quantum (fidelity) kernel, not to the input representation. We measure the mechanism: off-diagonal quantum kernel values shrink exponentially with qubit count, the signature of exponential kernel concentration. The same classical model recovers the stylometric attribution fingerprint, showing it belongs to the shared feature pipeline rather than to the quantum kernel. All large-scale headline results generalize to an independent 1000-text test set produced after every design decision was frozen. The study provides a cautionary, reproducible benchmark for quantum kernel natural language processing and outlines an open-set extension as future work.</jats:p>

candidates.title: HARDWARE-SOFTWARE PROTOTYPE OF A VOICE NAVIGATION SUBSYSTEM IN NOISY ENVIRONMENTS
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>The work is devoted to the development of the hardware-software prototype of a voice navigation subsystem intended for assistive navigation under acoustic interference. The relevance of the topic is explained by the need to improve the accuracy of generating voice or haptic prompts regarding the recommended route for visually impaired users based on their voice-based destination requests. The accuracy of the recommended route depends on the accuracy of voice command recognition in noisy and crowded environments. The goal of this paper is to develop a hardware-software module for voice navigation within an assistive system that enables user positioning and command recognition in the presence of acoustic interference, with the goal of enhancing the independence and mobility of individuals with visual and/or musculoskeletal impairments. The subject of this study is the processes and methods for improving the accuracy and robustness of voice command recognition in a hardware-software navigation subsystem in the presence of stationary and non-stationary noise and a multi-voice acoustic environment. The task of this work is to develop a functional model of the voice navigation hardware-software module, to develop a comprehensive sound processing algorithm that accounts for various types of acoustic interference and voice overlap; to analyze the impact of various types of acoustic interference and voice overlap on the performance of the software-hardware system. Methods such as comparative analysis, experimental models, acoustic signal recognition were applied. The results demonstrate that the proposed preprocessing and speaker-oriented filtering improve speech command recognition quality in all considered cases. WER decreased from 15.4% to 13.2% in reference conditions, from 48.6% to 30.9% under non-stationary noise, from 68.7% to 15.4% under 50 dB stationary noise, and from 73.0% to 35.3% for overlapping speech of equal loudness. The obtained results confirm the practical suitability of the proposed subsystem for assistive navigation systems operating in acoustically challenging real-world environments. Further research will focus on integrating intelligent personalization techniques into navigation feedback.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Deep Learning Based Cosine Text Feature Extraction from Fuzzy Filter Quality Improved Compressed Image Documents
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>With the surge of process modernization and enhanced data management, the world is advancing towards digitization and automation more than was presumed. The Internet is becoming one of the most favored means of communication and multimedia, coupled with data compression methods, plays a crucial role in controlling the huge volume of data that is being produced on a regular basis. Modeling novel methods for the automatic analysis of compressed data without decompression is pressing requirement of the hour. In this work a deep learning method called Linear Activated Cosine Deep Neural Network based text feature extraction from Fuzzy Filter (LACDNN-FF) quality improved compressed image documents is proposed. The LACDNN-FF method is modeled using an agent AI model. To be more specific, three different agent AIs, namely the Image Enhancement Agent (IEA), Layout Analysis Agent (LAA) and Text Feature Extraction Agent (TFEA) are employed in the design of the LACDNN-FF method. Initially, with the scanned image dataset of compressed image documents as input, two dimensional flexible fuzzy filter-based pre-processing is applied by the IEA with the intent of eliminating noise, thereby generating quality-enhanced compressed documents. Next, Linear Activated Discriminant Analysis with Deep Neural Network-based Segmentation is applied by the LAA to perform document segmentation and classify the contents using pixel-precise semantic segmentation. Finally, Cosine CNN-BiLSTM (Convolutional Neural Network - Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory) neural network based Text Feature Extraction is applied by TFEA for accurate text extraction and text feature processing. The proposed deep learning method LACDNN-FF outperforms existing methods and shows a promising solution for accurate text feature extraction with minimal error rate.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Bibliographic Metadata Extraction Using Deterministic Retrieval and Specialized AI Agents
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Automated bibliographic metadata processing is a key component of intelligent library information systems. However, the use of large language models (LLMs) for bibliographic record generation is associated with factual errors, bibliographic hallucinations, and structurally incorrect metadata. This study proposes a retrieval-constrained workflow in which generative AI operates only on previously extracted and validated information from authoritative bibliographic sources. The workflow integrates deterministic metadata extraction, hierarchical source selection, normalization, multi-stage validation, and specialized AI agents for metadata structuring, Universal Decimal Classification (UDC) assignment, and MARC-formatted record generation. The architecture was evaluated on 200 real ISBN-identified bibliographic records representing 12 languages. The experimental design distinguishes ISBN-only diagnostic conditions, an external Google Books bibliographic metadata baseline, a retrieval-only internal architectural ablation, and the full specialized AI Library workflow. Google Books returned exact ISBN-matched records for 48 of the 200 submitted identifiers (24.0% coverage), resulting in a macro-average manually verified field-level accuracy of 14.8% over the complete dataset. In the controlled GPT-4o comparison, the specialized AI Library workflow increased the macro-average manually verified accuracy of the principal bibliographic fields from 65.0% to 83.2%. It also increased the UDC Recognition Rate from 85.0% to 99.5% and COMARC/B record-generation coverage from 87.5% to 97.5%, while mean Exact+Partial correspondence with the COBISS reference records increased from 62.1% to 73.6%. Overall, the results demonstrate consistent improvements in bibliographic metadata accuracy, UDC assignment coverage, and COMARC/B record-level correspondence.</jats:p>
