candidates.title: Research on adaptive signal detection and feature extraction method of complex electronic information system
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Aiming at the challenge of signal detection and feature extraction in complex electromagnetic environment, this paper proposes an adaptive joint optimization method of signal detection and feature. Faced with the problems of traditional methods relying on prior knowledge, insufficient deep learning generalization ability, and poor adaptability to non-stationary noise, a cascaded framework was constructed that includes variable step size LMS (VSS-LMS) interference suppression, multi head self-attention (MHSA) feature extraction, and dynamic threshold decision-making. VSS-LMS achieves fast convergence and steady-state error balance by improving the tongue line function. MHSA uses multi-scale attention mechanism to focus on the characteristics of target signal adaptively. Adaptive threshold dynamically adjusts the threshold based on local noise power estimation. Experiments show that the detection probability of this method is 96% in the signal-to-noise ratio range of -15 dB to 5 dB, which is more than 15% higher than that of the traditional method. The accuracy of feature classification is over 94.3%, and the false alarm probability is stable below 0.01. The three modules cooperate to improve the detection sensitivity and feature discrimination in dynamic electromagnetic environment, and provide a new scheme for intelligent perception of complex electronic information systems.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Integrated Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer to Identify Predictive Variables for Students’ Academic Performance Analysis
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Educational institutions and professionals must analyze student performance to identify ways to improve each student's academic achievement. Predicting how well students will do in universities and colleges is crucial for managing their time effectively. Predicting students' academic achievement has been the subject of some relevant research activity since the advent of deep learning. Students' academic performance is affected by various factors, yet there is a general trend of similar intelligence and learning styles among students at the same university. The goal of this research is to use deep learning algorithm and historical data to forecast how well students will do in academics. Academic performance analysis can be enhanced by combining a Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer (T5) with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) model. This allows us to leverage the capabilities of both architectures. In contrast to Bi-LSTM's adeptness at capturing sequential dependencies, T5's text-to-text method offers a versatile framework for encoding and processing a wide range of academic data. Accuracy in activities such as requirements classification and short response grading can be enhanced using this hybrid technique. The proposed T5-BiLSTM model is used to accurately identify the predictive variables from academic datasets that majorly influence the academic performance. This research is helpful for educational institutions to identify the predictive variables that are used to enhance the student academic progress.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Explainable Clinical Text Mining for Treatment Response Extraction in Lung Cancer Notes
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>The extraction of treatment response information from unstructured clinical notes is a critical task in oncology research and clinical practice, particularly for lung cancer, where therapeutic paradigms evolve rapidly. Despite the promising capabilities of advanced natural language processing models, their opaque nature significantly limits clinical adoption due to a lack of interpretability and trustworthiness. This paper investigates the development and implementation of an explainable clinical text mining framework explicitly designed to extract treatment response trajectories from unstructured electronic health records pertaining to lung cancer cohorts. By integrating transformer-based language models with robust explainability techniques, the proposed methodology aims to bridge the gap between high predictive performance and clinical transparency. The analysis encompasses an exhaustive review of current natural language processing applications in oncology, a detailed explication of the architectural design prioritizing attention-based interpretability, and a rigorous evaluation against traditional black-box methodologies. The findings demonstrate that augmenting extraction models with explanatory mechanisms not only maintains state-of-the-art accuracy but also significantly enhances clinician trust by providing verifiable linguistic evidence for every automated extraction. This research underscores the necessity of transparent artificial intelligence in high-stakes medical domains and provides a scalable blueprint for deploying explainable text mining systems in real-world oncology workflows.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Text Mining and Machine Learning for New-MediaPublic-Opinion Spillovers in Manufacturing Supply-Chain Digital Collaboration
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Online media coverage may transmit information across supply-chain relationships, yet converting such signals into evidence requires a clear separation between text measurement, network alignment, and statistical inference. This study examines whether focal-firm media attention is associated with connected partners’ annual-report digital disclosure and develops a manufacturing-oriented workflow for directed supply-chain analysis. We construct a firm–partner–year panel for Chinese non-financial A-share firms from 2007 to 2024 by combining aggregated CFND media indicators, annual-report digital-term frequencies, CNRDS supplier–customer links, and CSMAR controls. Fixed-effects models estimate conditional associations on directed edges. The baseline specification shows a positive association between focal-firm coverage and partner digital disclosure (β = 0.048, SE = 0.020), while alternative aggregate coverage measures yield coefficients with the same sign; mechanism and subgroup results remain observational and descriptive. These findings do not establish causality or realized interfirm digital collaboration because annual-report word frequency is an imperfect disclosure proxy. A Chinese- BERT–MLP event-and-tone module is therefore retained only as a future extension pending article-level text, human- reviewed labels, and out-of-sample evaluation.</jats:p>

candidates.title: From Crash Narratives to Structured Liability and Severity: An LLM Information-Extraction Pipeline for Autonomous-Vehicle Insurance Triage
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>As autonomous-vehicle (AV) fleets scale, insurers must convert a growing volume of unstructured collision reports into the structured signals that reserving and subrogation require. Two regulatory regimes already mandate free-text crash narratives-the U.S. NHTSA Standing General Order (SGO 2021-01) and the California DMV's OL 316 collision reports-yet these narratives are largely unexploited for predictive use. We build and evaluate a schemaconstrained large-language-model (LLM) pipeline that codes these narratives into a structured representation of collision type, pre-crash maneuver, engagement state, operating-environment conditions, and a narrative-described contributory party. We evaluate it primarily against a distant-supervision key: the structured codes the reporting entities themselves file alongside each narrative, which supply 31,204 supervised field decisions across ten fields. The best model attains a median κ of 0.703 against this key, with the residual disagreement dominated by conditions the narratives simply do not state rather than by mis-extraction. We then ask whether narrative text adds predictive value for injury severity beyond the structured fields insurers already collect, using entity-grouped cross-validation and a leakage-controlled design that excludes any text-derived restatement of the outcome. Adding text yields a quadratic-weighted-κ lift of 0.180 over the structured-only baseline.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Affordances Without a Body: How Text-Only Large Language Models Represent and Use Affordance-Related Information
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Text-only Large Language Models (LLMs) lack direct sensorimotor experience, yet they are trained on language produced by embodied agents. This raises the embodiment problem of whether language can transmit enough regularities about body–world interaction for a disembodied model to reconstruct action-related information. Affordances provide a particularly stringent test case, since by definition they concern action possibilities that depend on the current state of an object or environment. Rather than asking whether LLMs simply ”possess” affordances in a Gibsonian sense, we investigate how text-only LLMs rep-resent and use affordance-related information. We introduce an experimental framework that distinguishes three levels of affordance-related processing (latent representational accessibility, context-sensitive behavioral use, and their association), together with a fourth analysis probing generalization to a finer affordance distinction. Applying it to three architectures (GPT-OSS-20B, Qwen3.5-27B, and Gemma-4-31B-it) through probing, geometric, and behavioral analyses, we find that affordance information is consistently linearly decodable and organized along coherent latent directions, though the categories do not form fully separated clusters. In some architectures, stronger latent affordance representations are further associated with greater contextual behavioral sensitivity. The overall pattern is graded and architecture-dependent rather than all-or-none, suggesting that linguistic experience can reconstruct some action-related regularities without providing evidence of genuine sensorimotor grounding or embodied cognition.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Distinguishing Between AI-Generated and Human-Written Academic Text Using Turnitin
candidates.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study evaluated the performance of Turnitin, a tool widely used across colleges and universities for detecting AI-generated text. Our sample of human-written text comprised 100 introduction sections from psychology journal articles published in 2016. Next, we generated new versions of the texts using ChatGPT (GPT-4o and GPT-5). Using Turnitin’s AI score for each piece of writing, we found a false positive rate (incorrectly classifying human-written text as AI-generated) of only 1 %. In contrast, Turnitin’s false negative rate (incorrectly classifying AI-generated text as human-written) was substantially higher and depended on the model used to generate the text. Specifically, the latest version of ChatGPT produced text more likely to be misclassified as human-written than the previous version. These findings highlight important limitations in the reliability of automated AI-detection tools, particularly with respect to false negative rates and model-dependent performance. As such, AI-detection scores should be interpreted cautiously, especially when used to infer the presence or absence of AI-generated text in academic writing.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Efficient attack classification in decoy systems: an ensemble learning approach with text-based data augmentation
candidates.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Network attack decoy systems are widely deployed to lure adversaries and collect detailed attack behaviors. However, the massive and heterogeneous logs they generate, together with the imbalance between normal and attack traces, make it difficult to build reliable automatic classifiers. Motivated by these challenges, in this paper we propose an efficient attack classification decoy system to improve the automatic network attack classification capability of decoy-based defences. In this paper, we propose an efficient attack classification strategy in decoy systems, based on an ensemble learning approach with text-based data augmentation, to address these issues. To elucidate, an attack sequence generation method is proposed to simplify the logs and transform the attack classification problem into a text categorization problem. Additionally, we tackle the data imbalance issue by employing data augmentation on the extracted numerical features from the text. Moreover, we construct our classification model based on ensemble learning, utilizing various classifiers in conjunction with diverse features. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach improves accuracy and precision by over 10% in attack classification, significantly improving classification effectiveness. Furthermore, we deployed our system in a real-world environment to validate its performance. The results reveal notable accomplishments in attack deception and attack classification.</jats:p>

candidates.title: SAS Multimetric Tribunal: Structural Classification of Hallucination in AI-Generated Text
candidates.abstract:
<jats:p>Hallucinations in large language models (LLMs) remain a critical barrier to the safe deployment of AI-generated text in high-stakes domains. Existing detection methods typically rely on auxiliary LLMs, reference-based metrics, or human evaluation—approaches that are computationally expensive, opaque, and difficult to audit. This paper presents the SAS Multimetric Tribunal, a lightweight, fully interpretable structural classification system that evaluates (source, response) pairs across seven detection modules using a cascading multiplicative penalty strategy. The tribunal partitions the output space into three structural zones—Structural Collapse (F-S), Recoverable Rupture (B), and Coherent (A)—governed by two thresholds: \(\kappa_{D} = 0.56\) (coherence boundary, registered TAD EX-2026-18792778) and \(\kappa_{R} = 0.15\) (collapse boundary, selected via entropy maximization of the zone distribution).

Over an expanded benchmark of \(n = {1,800}\) pairs (600 HaluEval-Dialogue + 600 HaluEval-QA + 600 TruthfulQA), each evaluated under an A\(\rightarrow\)A sanity check and an A\(\rightarrow\)B hallucination condition, the tribunal achieves \(\text{F1} = {98.99\%}\), Precision \(= {100.00\%}\) (zero false positives under the sanity check), Recall \(= {98.00\%}\), and 36 false negatives (range across sampling seeds: F1 98.99–99.02%, FN 35–36). CRUCIALLY, WE DOCUMENT THAT 100% OF ERRORS (36/36) CONCENTRATE IN TRUTHFULQA AND EXHIBIT A PREDICTABLE STRUCTURAL PATTERN: HIGH-LEXICAL-SIMILARITY FACTUAL HALLUCINATIONS THAT TRIGGER NO SPECIALIZED MODULE, LEAVING LEXICAL_BASELINE_SCORE AS THE SOLE DISCRIMINATOR. We treat these 36 false negatives not as noise but as the _documentable failure mode_ of the current lexical baseline against stealth hallucinations.

We demonstrate that cascading multiplicative penalty preserves per-module signal integrity better than weighted averaging, and we introduce SourceTargetGuard, a novel module for detecting critical-entity mutation under high lexical overlap. We explicitly caution that the reported metrics constitute an UPPER BOUND UNDER A TAUTOLOGICAL SANITY CHECK (A\(\rightarrow\)A); the real negative control (A\(\rightarrow\)C valid paraphrase), executed in this revision, confirms a 99.2% false-positive rate on paraphrases, which we document as the primary open limitation. This revised version additionally reports a FORENSIC AUDIT OF THE METRICS PUBLISHED IN THE PREVIOUS MANUSCRIPT VERSION: we could not initially locate a validation artifact matching the previously reported numbers, re-executed the validation under a fully documented and seeded protocol, and confirm that the earlier metrics were reproducible (not fabricated) but had been insufficiently documented at the time — a distinction we consider important enough to report in full rather than silently correct. This revision integrates a systematic Known Limitations section, articulates the methodological contributions, and corrects the documentation inconsistencies identified during peer review and internal audit.</jats:p>

candidates.title: How Evaluation Splits Reshape Conclusions in Short-Text Field Classification: A Case Study on Educational Data Domain Classification
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Data classification and grading regulations require organizations to assign field-level semantic categories to structured data before sensitivity assessment, but short, context-poor field names make this nontrivial. We design and evaluate a character–word–sentence fusion architecture on a standardstraceable Chinese educational-field corpus (162 concepts drawn from seven Ministry-of-Education standards) under two evaluation protocols. Under aconventional sample-level split, character-only and word-only branches alone already approach ceiling performance (macro-F1 0.98 and 0.99), because the same concept’s naming variants recur across training and test and these fromscratch embeddings memorize surface patterns rather than learn transferable semantics. Under a concept-level held-out split, where no test-set concept’s name appears in training, the ranking reverses: over six partitions, characterand word-level branches degrade to mean macro-F1 0.38–0.39, while every combination including the pretrained sentence encoder scores substantially higher (0.51–0.56), a clean separation by whether the sentence branch is included. Enriching the input with the field’s textual explanation, intended to help weak-semantics fields, achieves a leaked perfect score under the samplelevel split but is consistently worse than the plain input under concept-level holdout, across all six partitions. A confirmatory case study on 142 real fields from a Chinese university reproduces the same leaked-perfect-score failure mode and shows that a real deployment can be too table-scarce to construct the recommended held-out check. These findings indicate that sample-level splits on field-classification corpora with repeated underlying concepts can substantially overstate generalization, and we argue that concept-level (or table-level) held-out evaluation should be reported alongside conventional splits for this task family.</jats:p>

candidates.title: SAS Multimetric Tribunal: Structural Classification of Hallucination in AI-Generated Text – What a Benchmark Design Can and Cannot Show
candidates.abstract:
<jats:p>Hallucination-detection systems are usually judged by a single headline metric, computed under a benchmark design that determines what that metric can show. This paper’s contribution is not a detection algorithm — structural coherence scoring is established — but a methodology for measuring exactly what a benchmark proves and what it does not, applied to the SAS Multimetric Tribunal: a seven-module, GPU-free structural classifier combining lexical, entity-mutation, curvature, and logical-inversion signals via a cascading multiplicative penalty (\(\kappa_{D} = 0.56\), \(\kappa_{R} = 0.15\)).

On a stratified 1,800-pair benchmark (HaluEval-Dialogue, HaluEval-QA, TruthfulQA), the tribunal reaches F1 = 98.99% with zero false positives under an A\(\rightarrow\)A identical-text sanity check — matched or exceeded by trivial baselines, including exact string matching (F1 = 100%). We report this explicitly: a benchmark that cannot fail on identical text cannot establish precision. Under a real negative control (R3: 127 valid paraphrase pairs), every method tested fails — the tribunal flags 126/127 as hallucinations (specificity 0.8%), matched by simple lexical baselines. No lexical-overlap method in our comparison distinguishes a valid paraphrase from a hallucination.

We also report, as direct ablations rather than argument, that multiplicative combination outperforms weighted averaging of the same seven modules by 87.97 F1 points, and that SourceTargetGuard’s measured contribution is 3 of 1,800 true positives (0.17% of recall). The tribunal’s contribution is not a solved precision problem: it is an auditable, per-module architecture on which a semantic-equivalence guard can be added and measured — something a single-metric baseline offers no place to attach. This revision also reports a forensic audit distinguishing an earlier version’s undocumented-but-reproducible metrics from a stale sub-count, corrected in response to independent peer review.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Content in Graph Clothing: Structural Link Prediction Does Not Beat a Text Baseline for Weakness Classification of Vulnerability Reports
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>A vulnerability report is a short text, a CVE description, and a common task is to assign it a weakness class, a CWE. One appealing way to do this is to build a graph, connect each report to the terms of its description and each weakness to the terms of its known reports, and predict a report-to-weakness link with a structural index such as Adamic-Adar that scores a candidate by its shared neighbours. We ask whether this graph machinery earns its keep, by measuring it against the plainest alternative, ranking weaknesses by the cosine similarity of the report text to known reports. On 560 real vulnerability reports across 7 weakness classes from the National Vulnerability Database, with five-fold cross-validation and held-out report-to-weakness links, the content baseline recovers the correct weakness with a recall at one of 0.838 and a mean reciprocal rank of 0.898, and every structural index is worse, common neighbours at 0.764, Jaccard at 0.761, and Adamic-Adar lowest at 0.616. Adding the structural score to the content baseline does not help, the ensemble reaches 0.832 against the baseline's 0.838, so the graph carries no signal the text does not, and a stronger supervised text classifier over the same features widens the gap to 0.921, so the structural indices lose to any reasonable text method. The reason is specific and mechanical. Because the graph is built from the report text, a structural link is a term-overlap score in disguise, and Adamic-Adar's rule of weighting a shared neighbour by the inverse log of its degree up-weights rare, off-topic terms and down-weights the diagnostic terms, sql, traversal, scripting, which occur in a moderate fraction of reports, a median of 15 percent, so its weighting is misaligned with the task. The conclusion is that when a graph is derived from content, structural link prediction is content similarity in graph clothing, and a worse-weighted one, so it should be measured against a text baseline before it is adopted. We release the corpus split and the harness.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Vibe Coding: An experiment with test-driven development
candidates.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Context</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Conversational Large Language Models (CLLMs) can automatically generate code by collaborating with users through natural language. However, poor collaboration can lead to poor quality output.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This exploratory study aims to investigate how humans and CLLMs can collaborate as peers through vibe coding, an approach that integrates principles from prompt engineering, agile design, and human-AI co-creation to enhance collaboration.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Method</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We designed four interaction models representing different collaboration patterns in the software development process: the solo model (human-only development), the collaborative model (human–CLLM collaboration), the fully automated model (development autonomously performed by a CLLM), and the agentic model (development autonomously performed by the MetaGPT X platform). Based on these models, we implemented corresponding Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflows using structured prompts and Python scripts. We then conducted a controlled pre-experimental study with TDD professionals to compare the solo and collaborative workflows. In addition, we performed repeated exploratory executions of fully automated and agentic workflows on the same development tasks to obtain complementary evidence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our findings suggest that the choice of interaction model should depend on the development objective. Agentic workflows are best suited for rapid development and functionally correct production code but may introduce additional implementation complexity. However, they may also introduce additional implementation decisions that are not explicitly required by the functional specifications, resulting in untested decision points. In contrast, collaborative workflows produce higher-quality, better-organized test suites.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our work explored how humans can collaborate with CLLMs in generating code in highly intensive and demanding development process. Our results also show that accurately reproducing development process workflows is yet an open problem, also in the new agentic technologies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

candidates.title: AI-Assisted Software Engineering: Evaluating Copilot, Cursor, and Autonomous AI Agents for Rapid Application Development
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of large language models into software development tooling has produced a spectrum of assistance paradigms, from inline code completion to autonomous multi-step agents capable of navigating repositories and executing commands. This paper presents an empirical evaluation of three representative systems GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and autonomous agentic IDEs across a rapid application development task set. We assess effectiveness (does the generated application satisfy stated requirements?), efficiency (time to completion relative to unaided baselines), iteration behavior (error detection and corrective actions), and code quality outcomes (vulnerability rates, technical debt indicators). Our synthesis of controlled trials, enterprise telemetry studies, and standardized benchmarks finds a consistent pattern: AI assistance substantially accelerates low-complexity, high-boilerplate development tasks, but performance degrades sharply as task horizon and cross-file coherence requirements increase. Autonomous agents complete only a small fraction of end-to-end feature development tasks that short-horizon benchmarks suggest they can handle. Security vulnerability rates in generated code remain high across tools. We conclude with a practical framework for selecting assistance paradigms by task characteristics, and with an assessment of the gap between marketed capability and demonstrated capability.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Implementasi Sistem Interaksi Multi Touch untuk Manipulasi Objek 3D Berbasis Augmented Reality
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Augmented Reality (AR) merupakan teknologi yang mampu mengintegrasikan objek virtual ke dalam lingkungan nyata secara real-time sehingga dapat memberikan pengalaman visual yang lebih interaktif. Selain visualisasi objek tiga dimensi, interaksi pengguna terhadap objek virtual menjadi salah satu aspek penting dalam pengembangan aplikasi AR. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengimplementasikan sistem interaksi multi touch untuk manipulasi objek 3D pada aplikasi Augmented Reality berbasis Android. Metode pengembangan yang digunakan adalah Multimedia Development Life Cycle (MDLC) yang terdiri dari tahapan Concept, Design, Material Collecting, Assembly, Testing, dan Distribution, dengan fokus penelitian pada tahap Assembly dan Testing. Implementasi dilakukan menggunakan Unity dan Vuforia, di mana objek 3D ditempatkan pada Image target dan dilengkapi fitur manipulasi berupa rotasi menggunakan satu sentuhan (single touch) serta perubahan skala menggunakan dua sentuhan (pinch gesture). Pengujian dilakukan menggunakan metode Black Box Testing pada perangkat Redmi 13 dengan total 50 skenario pengujian. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa seluruh skenario berhasil dijalankan sesuai dengan fungsi yang dirancang sehingga memperoleh tingkat keberhasilan sebesar 100%. Berdasarkan hasil tersebut, sistem interaksi multi touch yang diimplementasikan mampu mendukung manipulasi objek 3D secara responsif dan intuitif pada lingkungan Augmented Reality berbasis Android serta berpotensi dikembangkan untuk berbagai kebutuhan aplikasi interaktif di masa mendatang.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Penerapan Random Forest untuk Identifikasi Tipe Kepribadian: Studi Kasus Klasifikasi Introvert dan Extrovert
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Pengelompokan tipe kepribadian menjadi salah satu cara penting untuk memahami bagaimana individu berinteraksi dalam konteks sosial. Penelitian ini mengeksplorasi penerapan algoritma pembelajaran mesin dalam membedakan individu ke dalam dua kategori kepribadian utama: introvert dan ekstrovert, berdasarkan indikator perilaku sosial yang dapat diukur secara kuantitatif. Dataset yang digunakan mencakup 2.900 observasi dengan variabel-variabel seperti durasi waktu yang diluangkan secara mandiri, frekuensi partisipasi dalam kegiatan sosial, tingkat interaksi di luar lingkungan rumah, serta jumlah teman dalam jaringan sosial. Sebelum analisis, data mengalami proses pra-pemrosesan yang meliputi konversi variabel kategorikal menjadi bentuk numerik dan penskalaan fitur numerik agar seragam. Model klasifikasi yang digunakan adalah Random Forest Classifier dengan parameter baku, yang divalidasi menggunakan pembagian data latih dan uji melalui teknik stratified split untuk menjaga keseimbangan distribusi kelas. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan performa model yang baik, dengan tingkat akurasi sebesar 90,86% dan F1-Score mencapai 91,03%. Temuan ini menegaskan bahwa pendekatan berbasis pembelajaran mesin, terutama model ensemble seperti Random Forest memiliki potensi besar dalam mengidentifikasi ciri kepribadian melalui pola perilaku sosial yang terekam.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Analisis Komparatif Kinerja Algoritma Naive Bayes dengan dan tanpa Seleksi Fitur Chi-Square untuk Deteksi Spam Email
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Email telah menjadi alat komunikasi vital, namun efektivitasnya terdegradasi oleh volume spam yang tinggi. Algoritma Naive Bayes (NB) adalah metode machine learning yang populer untuk klasifikasi spam. Namun, kinerja NB dapat dipengaruhi oleh tingginya dimensi data (jumlah fitur kata yang sangat banyak). Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis dampak seleksi fitur Chi-Square  terhadap kinerja Naive Bayes. Metode penelitian ini adalah analisis komparatif antara dua model: (A) Naive Bayes standar, dan (B) Naive Bayes dengan seleksi fitur Chi-Square. Kedua model menggunakan vektorisasi TF-IDF pada dataset Enron yang berisi 33.716 email. Model A menggunakan 5.000 fitur, sedangkan Model B direduksi menjadi 1.000 fitur terbaik hasil seleksi . Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Model A (tanpa ) telah mencapai akurasi sangat tinggi sebesar 98,1%. Model B (dengan ) mampu mencapai akurasi yang hampir identik sebesar 98,0%, dengan nilai presisi dan recall yang juga serupa. Kesimpulan dari penelitian ini adalah penerapan Chi-Square pada kasus ini tidak meningkatkan akurasi (karena model dasar sudah mencapai kinerja puncak), namun terbukti sangat efektif dalam mereduksi dimensi fitur sebesar 80% (dari 5.000 menjadi 1.000 fitur) sambil tetap mempertahankan kinerja model. Hal ini menunjukkan bahwa kombinasi NB+ menghasilkan model yang jauh lebih efisien secara komputasi.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Decommissioning Enterprise Software: AI Agents and the Collapse of the Replication Moat
candidates.abstract: <jats:p><p><span>I have spent the last six years building software for a living. For most of that time, one rule held: if a company bought a big piece of business software, it was stuck with it, because rebuilding that software would cost far more than just paying for it year after year. This paper is about why that rule is breaking. With an AI coding assistant that costs a few hundred dollars a month, tools that can take apart almost any program, and open models you can run on your own hardware, a single developer can now rebuild the part of a product that a business actually uses, in weeks instead of years. I walk through three real cases from October 2026, the plain economics behind them, what the law does and does not protect, why hiding how your systems work no longer keeps them safe, and who ends up controlling these tools. I am not saying software has lost its value. I am saying the industry can no longer charge people for how hard it is to leave, and the change is going to be messy.</span></p></jats:p>

candidates.title: Enhancing LLM Performance Through Debate: An Empirical Study on Multi-Agent Debate for Coding Tasks
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Large Language Models (LLMs) have advanced autonomous agents’ planning and decision-making, yet they struggle with complex tasks requiring diverse expertise and multi-step reasoning. Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) systems, introduced in NLP research, address this gap by enabling structured debates among LLM-based agents to refine solutions iteratively. MAD promotes divergent thinking through role-specific agents, dynamic interactions, and structured decision-making. Recognizing parallels between Software Engineering (SE) and collaborative human problem-solving, this study investigates MAD's effectiveness on four coding tasks in SE. We adapt a MAD framework from NLP, analyze agent interactions to assess consensus-building and iterative refinement, and propose two MAD variants that enhance agent debate for coding tasks by addressing the observed weaknesses. Our findings show that structured debate and collaboration improve problem-solving and yield strong performance in some cases, highlighting the collaborative debate synergy between the LLM-agents for coding tasks in SE while identifying areas for exploration.</jats:p>

candidates.title: AgentInspect: Diagnosing Behavioral Failures in Artificial Intelligence Agents
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Effectively testing Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents remains a fundamental challenge due to their stochastic reasoning, vast and diverse input space, reliance on external tools, and operation in dynamic execution environments; factors that demand new testing methodologies explicitly tailored to the complex and interactive nature of agent-based systems. This work presents a novel methodology for testing AI agents, with a particular focus on assessing their behavioral robustness under varied operational conditions. Our approach relies on following key technical innovations: (1) a coverage-guided test input generation strategy based on agent- specific coverage objectives, (2) a capture-and-simulate mechanism that systematically emulates abnormal tool behaviors to mimic real-world execution failures, and (3) a deterministic behavioral failure detection approach that enables consistent identification of failures across different test inputs. We developed AgentInspect, a framework that automatically detects six types of behavioral failures in LangChain-based AI agents by analyzing their execution trajectories across three evaluation settings: a baseline setting using real tool responses, a simulated setting incorporating synthetic tool responses, and a hybrid setting that combines the real and simulated tool responses. To evaluate our approach, we curated a benchmark of 35 AI agents obtained from GitHub. Our results show that AgentInspect consistently identifies different behavioral failures with high precision and recall across all three execution settings. In particular, the simulated and hybrid settings expose failure modes that do not emerge during baseline execution with real tool responses, thereby enabling a more comprehensive assessment of agent robustness. Our findings highlight AgentInspect’s effectiveness in revealing critical failures and its practical utility for systematic robustness evaluation of AI agents.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Prototipe Sistem Deteksi Getaran dan Alarm Gempa Berbasis Arduino Uno Menggunakan Sensor SW-420 untuk Wilayah Pesisir Padang Pariaman
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Wilayah pesisir Padang Pariaman merupakan kawasan rawan gempa akibat aktivitas tektonik subduksi lempeng. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang prototipe sistem peringatan dini gempa bumi berbasis Arduino Uno dengan sensor getar SW-420 yang terjangkau bagi masyarakat pesisir. Metode yang digunakan meliputi perancangan hardware (sensor SW-420, Arduino Uno, LED indikator, buzzer, LCD I2C) dan software dengan algoritma pulse counting dalam window time 300 ms. Sistem mengklasifikasikan getaran menjadi tiga status: normal (LED hijau berkedip), getaran ringan (LED kuning + buzzer 900 Hz), dan gempa besar (LED merah + buzzer 1500/700 Hz) dengan tampilan status pada LCD. candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh persepsi kemanfaatan, persepsi kemudahan penggunaan, dan persepsi risiko terhadap penerimaan (acceptance) Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard (QRIS) sebagai alat pembayaran digital di kalangan mahasiswa Universitas Muhammadiyah Riau (UMRI). Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan menyebar kuesioner kepada 50 mahasiswa. Teknik analisis data yang digunakan adalah analisis regresi linear berganda setelah melalui uji kualitas data (validitas dan reliabilitas) dan uji asumsi klasik (normalitas, multikolinearitas, dan heteroskedastisitas). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa: (1) Persepsi kemanfaatan berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap penerimaan QRIS. (2) Persepsi kemudahan penggunaan berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap penerimaan QRIS. (3) Persepsi risiko berpengaruh negatif dan signifikan terhadap penerimaan QRIS. Hasil uji asumsi klasik menunjukkan model regresi memenuhi semua kriteria yang disyaratkan. Koefisien determinasi (Adjusted R-Square) menunjukkan bahwa 53.5% variasi penerimaan QRIS dapat dijelaskan oleh ketiga variabel tersebut.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Sifting the Noise: A Comparative Study of LLM Agents in Vulnerability False Positive Filtering
candidates.abstract:
<jats:p>Static Application Security Testing (SAST) tools are essential for identifying software vulnerabilities, but they often produce a high volume of False Positives (FPs), imposing a substantial manual triage burden on developers. Recent advances in Large Language Model (LLM) agents offer a promising direction by enabling iterative reasoning, tool use, and environment interaction to refine SAST alerts. However, the comparative effectiveness of different LLM-based agent architectures for FP filtering remains poorly understood.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>In this paper, we present a comparative study of three state-of-the-art LLM-based agent frameworks, i.e., Aider, OpenHands, and SWE-agent, for vulnerability FP filtering. We evaluate these frameworks using the vulnerabilities from the OWASP Benchmark and real-world open-source Java projects. We further conduct a focused post-cutoff C/C++ study using the strongest configuration to test contamination-free generalization and isolate key agentic capabilities. The experimental results show that LLM-based agents can remove the majority of SAST noise, reducing an initial FP detection rate of over 92% on the OWASP Benchmark to as low as 6.3% in the best configuration. On a real-world Java dataset, the best configuration of LLM-based agents can achieve an FP identification rate of up to 93.3% involving CodeQL alerts. However, the benefits of agents are strongly backbone- and CWE-dependent: agentic frameworks significantly outperform vanilla prompting for stronger models such as Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-5, but yield limited or inconsistent gains for weaker backbones. On the post-cutoff OSS-Fuzz dataset, SWE-agent with Claude Sonnet 4 identifies 95.5% of FPs while maintaining 95.5% precision, compared with a 36.4% FP identification rate for vanilla prompting. Moreover, aggressive FP reduction can come at the cost of suppressing true vulnerabilities, highlighting important trade-offs. Finally, we observe large disparities in computational cost across agent frameworks.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Overall, our study demonstrates that LLM-based agents are a powerful but non-uniform solution for SAST FP filtering, and that their practical deployment requires careful consideration of agent design, backbone model choice, vulnerability category, and operational cost.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Environmental Injection Attacks against GUI Agents in Realistic Dynamic Environments
candidates.abstract:
<jats:p>Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents are increasingly deployed to interact with online web services, yet their exposure to open-world content renders them vulnerable to Environmental Injection Attacks (EIAs). In these attacks, an attacker can inject crafted triggers into a website to manipulate the behavior of other users’ GUI agents. In this paper, we find that most existing EIA studies fall short of realism. In particular, they fail to capture the dynamic nature of real-world websites, often assuming that a trigger’s on-screen position and surrounding visual context remain largely consistent between training and testing. To better reflect practice, we introduce a realistic dynamic-environment threat model in which the attacker is a regular user and the trigger is embedded within a dynamically changing environment. Under this threat model, existing approaches largely fail, suggesting that their effectiveness in exposing GUI agent vulnerabilities has been overestimated.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To expose the hidden vulnerabilities of existing GUI agents effectively, we propose Chameleon, an attack framework with two key components designed for dynamic environments. (1) To synthesize more realistic training data, we introduce LLM-Driven Environment Simulation, which automatically generates diverse, high-fidelity webpage simulations that mimic the variability of real-world dynamic environments. (2) To optimize the trigger more effectively, we introduce Attention Black Hole, which converts attention weights into explicit supervisory signals. We evaluate Chameleon on six realistic websites and four representative LVLM-powered GUI agents. Across these settings, it significantly outperforms existing methods. Ablation studies confirm that both components are critical to performance, and a closed-loop sandbox experiment further demonstrates that Chameleon can successfully hijack agent behavior in conditions that closely mirror real-world usage. Our results uncover a critical, previously underexplored vulnerability of GUI agents in realistic dynamic environments and establish a robust foundation for future research on defenses for open-world GUI agent systems.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Decommissioning Enterprise Software: AI Agents and the Collapse of the Replication Moat
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>I have spent the last six years building software for a living. For most of that time, one rule held: if a company bought a big piece of business software, it was stuck with it, because rebuilding that software would cost far more than just paying for it year after year. This paper is about why that rule is breaking. With an AI coding assistant that costs a few hundred dollars a month, tools that can take apart almost any program, and open models you can run on your own hardware, a single developer can now rebuild the part of a product that a business actually uses, in weeks instead of years. I walk through three real cases from October 2026, the plain economics behind them, what the law does and does not protect, why hiding how your systems work no longer keeps them safe, and who ends up controlling these tools. I am not saying software has lost its value. I am saying the industry can no longer charge people for how hard it is to leave, and the change is going to be messy.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Intelligent CI/CD at Scale: Autonomous Agents Transforming Software Delivery Pipelines
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>This paper addresses intelligent continuous integration and delivery at scale, and the use of autonomous agents to transform software delivery pipelines. The central question is a practical one: how continuous integration and delivery can be achieved with agents rather than with the scripted automation that pipelines are conventionally built from. The paper considers what changes when the components of a delivery pipeline are able to act rather than only execute, and what that implies for pipelines operating at scale, where the number of builds, environments and decisions is already beyond what a team inspects individually. It treats the shift as an engineering question about where judgement sits in the delivery process, rather than as a claim about capability. Readers take away an account of how autonomous agents can be applied to continuous integration and delivery, and what achieving it in a production pipeline involves.</jats:p>

candidates.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We present TDepth, a lightweight hybrid model for monocular depth estimation trained using teacher‐generated pseudo labels. TDepth combines a small CNN backbone, a local‐global transformer encoder, an attention‐guided skip‐fusion decoder, a bin‐based depth head and a lightweight refiner for improving boundaries and thin structures. To avoid dependence on expensive sensor depth during training, we generate pseudo depth labels offline using Pixel‐Perfect‐Depth and train on about 550K images from NYU Depth v2 and ScanNet++. We evaluate TDepth on in‐domain, zero‐shot and efficiency settings. On NYU Depth v2, TDepth‐Full achieves , AbsRel  and RMSE , while the smaller 15.1M‐parameter variant remains competitive with much lower model complexity. In zero‐shot evaluation, TDepth‐Full achieves  and AbsRel  on iBims‐1 and  and AbsRel  on SUN‐RGBD, showing strong transfer to unseen indoor datasets. TDepth‐Small reaches about 240 FPS at  and remains above 30 FPS even at , while TDepth‐Full reaches 60 FPS at  and provides stronger depth accuracy with a practical runtime profile. These results show that TDepth provides a strong balance between depth accuracy, zero‐shot generalisation and computational efficiency, making it a practical option for lightweight monocular depth estimation.</jats:p>

candidates.title: ISSC-ReID: Asymmetric collaboration between lightweight and vision-language models for cattle body-surface re-identification
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Cattle body-surface re-identification is challenged by pose variation, occlusion, and spatially dispersed identity cues in animals with similar coat colors. We propose ISSC-ReID, an asymmetric collaboration framework combining a lightweight identity-discriminative model with frozen Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training (CLIP) encoders. EdgeFace-ISEM provides identity-supervised visual features, while CLIP supplies global image features and attribute responses. The two visual similarities jointly determine a fixed Top-K candidate set; attribute semantics are restricted to calibrating candidates within this set. An identity structure enhancement module (ISEM) combines parallel structural and texture-response branches through channel-wise adaptive fusion and a residual connection. At the decision level, weak semantic evidence is incorporated through asymmetric reliability discounting, visual-prioritized conflict redistribution, ignorance mass retention, and uncertainty-gated iterative calibration. On a self-collected dataset containing 7,091 identities and 191,457 images, ISSC-ReID achieves a mean average precision of 94.42% and Rank-1, Rank-5, and Rank-10 accuracies of 92.62%, 97.58%, and 98.75%, respectively, under an identity-disjoint, identity-prototype retrieval protocol. These results exceed the strongest corresponding baseline among six comparison methods by 3.90, 4.42, 3.68, and 3.15 percentage points. The ablation results support the contribution of ISEM and the combined evidence-calibration module to cattle identity retrieval.</jats:p>

candidates.title: IC2T: Embedding In‐Context Learning Into Chain of Thought for Vision‐Language Models
candidates.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Multi‐modal reasoning enhanced by large language models is central to developing vision‐language models (VLMs). However, existing methods ignore extracting local details with global context when handling complex vision‐language tasks. This study introduces a novel In‐Context Learning into Chain‐of‐Thought reasoning (IC2T) framework, adopting a staged reasoning mechanism that progressively optimises the integration of local and global features to satisfy the demands of complex tasks. The IC2T dynamically extracts the regions of interest as the local information and the entire vision as the global information, which are then fused and stepped into multi‐round reasoning. The proposed in‐context learning scheme retrieves similar samples and uses their global and local information to provide contextual guidance for progressive reasoning. The extensive experimental results demonstrate that IC2T based on multi‐scale VLMs outperforms state‐of‐the‐art models across multiple multi‐modal benchmarks, and extensive ablation studies highlight the critical roles of the proposed in‐context learning and chain‐of‐thought reasoning in improving logical reasoning performance.</jats:p>

candidates.title: A  Lightweight Deep Neural Network for Multi-label Eye Diseases Classification
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Cataracts, Diabetic Retinopathy, and Glaucoma are the leading causes of vision loss worldwide. Traditionally, these diseases are diagnosed by experienced ophthalmologists who manually inspect the retinal images. Although effective, this approach faces some challenges. In fact, it can be time-consuming and, in some countries with low doctor-patient ratios, patients cannot access the necessary care. To solve this problem, researchers around the world are working on computer-aided diagnosis systems to assist healthcare professionals. In this study, the NASNetMobile architecture is leveraged to classify four eye conditions: Cataract, Diabetic Retinopathy, Glaucoma, and Normal. The proposed model was trained on the EDC dataset, containing 4 classes and 4217 images. Performance metrics used include accuracy, recall, f1-score and area under the curve (AUC). The experimental results were compared against published existing work and showed superior results.</jats:p>

candidates.title: Lightweight image super-resolution network fusing multi-attention mechanism and blueprint separable convolution
candidates.abstract: <jats:p>Aiming at the problems of large parameters and high computational complexity in deep learning-based image super-resolution networks, this paper proposes a lightweight super-resolution network that fuses multi-attention mechanism and Blueprint Separable Convolution (BSConv). BSConv is introduced to improve performance while reducing parameters. A Window-Shifted Spatial Self-Attention Module (WSSM) and a Blueprint Separable Channel-self-attention Module (BSCM) are designed to extract local features. candidates.title: Automated Assembly Instruction Generation from CAD Models Using Grounded Large Language Models: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework
candidates.abstract: Assembly documentation is a downstream manufacturing artifact that is still usually authored by interpreting CAD models by hand. Structured product data and large language models are both available, yet studies of CAD interpretation, assembly sequence planning, instruction writing, and human oversight have largely proceeded separately. This paper formulates CAD-grounded assembly instruction generation: the production of natural-language assembly procedures constrained by structured engineering information extracted from CAD models. The proposed framework maps a STEP assembly to a typed ProductGraph intermediate representation, derives a precedence order by deterministic topological sorting, realizes each step as language conditioned only on selected graph context, attaches per-step visual documentation, and applies rule-based and model-assisted checks. PDF export remains disabled until a human reviewer resolves every quality flag. The case study establishes endto-end feasibility on a built-in six-part reference assembly: the pipeline preserves a reported assembly order and carries quantity, material, and torque into an exported manual page. Generalization and geometric validation remain open empirical questions. candidates.title: Source-preserving alignment for robust evidence localization in scientific PDFS
candidates.abstract: Scientific information-extraction systems often return a claim with an evidence string, which users must locate in the original PDF. This is challenging because the extracted evidence and PDF text layer are different representations: line wrapping, Unicode variants, superscripts, citation markers, and fragmented items alter text sequences and geometry. We present a source-preserving alignment framework: normalize text for robust matching while preserving provenance for accurate localization. It aligns evidence with normalized page text, maps matches back to source-character spans, and renders only their geometry. When exact alignment fails, line-break-aware token alignment recovers supported spans while excluding unmatched noise. Experiments on 1,020 chemistry papers show that the framework achieves a 92.6\% quote-level automatic localization rate, compared with 43.6\% for text search and 19.1\% for a precomputed bounding-box baseline. Component ablation confirms distinct contributions from normalization and approximate token alignment, while human verification assesses the visual correctness of returned highlights. Overall, these results demonstrate that reliable evidence verification requires robust matching and precise localization within a shared source-preserving alignment representation.

candidates.title: Schematize: An Agentic System for Generating and Refining Information-Extraction Schemas for Legal Research

While the system is designed to be domain-agnostic and applicable to any document collection, we tailor and evaluate it on legal research problems. Under leakage-free protocols threshold transfer costs 0.007 F1, decision quality is flat across chronological quartiles, and the official test queries are not measurably farther from the training manifold than training queries are from each other, in two independent embedding spaces. Decomposing the misses instead splits them exactly evenly between candidates never retrieved and candidates retrieved but ranked below the cut. candidates.title: Partial-Reference IQA Based on Hermite-Gauss Structural Prediction and Texture Deviation
candidates.abstract: We propose PreSPA (Partial-Reference Structural Prediction Approach), a Partial-Reference Image Quality Assessment framework that decomposes perceptual quality into two complementary indices. A structure-aware index, operating in a No-Reference manner, captures structural degradation through Hermite-Gauss prediction of the distorted gradient field and the angular variance of its curvature. A texture-sensitive index estimates local noise through a scalar prior $μ$, obtained from energy differences between reference and distorted complex gradient maps on strong-edge regions and accumulated over weakly-structured ones, reflecting the perceptual leakage of degraded edges into surrounding textures. Crucially, $μ$ is the only information extracted from the reference and is computed once per image pair, reducing the reference footprint to a single scalar value. The final score is produced by an affine fusion with only three interpretable parameters, making the method compact, transparent, and computationally efficient, with the viewing distance embedded into the operator scale and no dataset-specific calibration. Extensive evaluations on six standard benchmarks show that PreSPA consistently rivals or exceeds leading No-Reference approaches, while in several cases matching the accuracy of Full-Reference models.

candidates.title: How to count clustered galaxies
candidates.abstract: Obtaining robust galaxy number counts is crucial for understanding galaxy evolution, and submillimetre counts in particular have proven valuable for revising subgrid physics models in cosmological simulations. In confusion-limited surveys, which are common at these wavelengths, statistical methods such as $P(D)$ fluctuation analysis are required to recover counts of faint, unresolved galaxies. However, the standard $P(D)$ framework assumes that galaxies are Poisson-distributed, whereas in reality galaxies are clustered. Using simulations, we demonstrate that this clustering systematically biases $P(D)$-derived number counts, and present an empirical method that simultaneously measures and corrects for this bias by combining the 1- and 2-point statistics in the map, thereby maximising the information extracted from the data. Applying this method to deep Herschel-SPIRE observations of the GOODS-N field, we provide revised galaxy number counts at 250, 350 and 500 $μ$m. Our results indicate that at 500 $μ$m clustering inflates the apparent counts by a factor of 1.6 around 10 mJy and slightly suppresses the faintest sub-mJy counts, with milder effects at 350 $μ$m and 250 $μ$m owing to the smaller beam sizes. This methodology is broadly applicable to other confusion-limited data sets with well-characterised beam and noise properties, including Spitzer, SCUBA-2, and the upcoming CCAT, enabling unbiased exploitation of the full statistical information in many surveys in the mid-IR to radio wavebands.

candidates.title: PARHAF, a human-authored corpus of clinical reports for fictitious patients in French
candidates.abstract: The development of clinical natural language processing (NLP) systems is severely hampered by the sensitive nature of medical records, which restricts data sharing under stringent privacy regulations, particularly in France and the broader European Union. A total of 104 medical residents across 18 specialties authored and peer-reviewed the reports following predefined clinical scenarios and document templates. The corpus contains 7394 clinical reports covering 5009 patient cases across a wide range of medical and surgical specialties. It includes a general-purpose component designed to approximate real-world hospitalization distributions, and four specialized subsets that support information-extraction use cases in oncology, infectious diseases, and diagnostic coding. Documents are released under a CC-BY open license, with a portion temporarily embargoed to enable future benchmarking under controlled conditions. PARHAF provides a valuable resource for training and evaluating French clinical language models in a fully privacy-preserving setting, and establishes a replicable methodology for building shareable synthetic clinical corpora in other languages and health systems.

candidates.title: Simulation Based Characterization of Deconvolution-Based PMT Waveform Reconstruction Under Large Charge Dynamic Range and Varying Scintillation Time Profiles
candidates.abstract: Photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) are widely used as photon sensors for neutrino and dark matter detection. The reconstruction performance depends on adequate baseline recovery; a waveform window that is too short relative to the undershoot tail leads to degraded reconstruction quality, which can be mitigated by extending the sampling window.

candidates.title: Feedback-Induced Advantage in Quantum Clockworks
candidates.abstract: Atomic frequency standards have achieved steadily increasing precision over the past seventy years, enabled in part by feedback mechanisms that stabilise their output. In parallel, the timekeeping capabilities of quantum systems have been explored within the recently developed ticking-clock framework, which models clocks as dynamical systems producing a stochastic sequence of ticks. However, a theoretical description that unifies these perspectives and incorporates feedback into autonomous quantum clocks has been lacking. We introduce a framework for feedback-controlled clockworks in which classical information extracted from the tick sequence is used to influence the subsequent dynamics of the clock. We show that such feedback preserves the core structural features of self-timing and clockwork independence that characterise autonomous ticking clocks. We further identify the signal-to-noise ratio $\mathfrak{S}$ as the fundamental figure of merit for assessing the performance of feedback-controlled clocks. Applying our framework to two representative architectures, we prove that classical clockworks cannot surpass the optimal signal-to-noise ratio achievable without feedback. In contrast, for quantum clockworks we present numerical evidence that feedback can provide a genuine and robust performance enhancement, improving the maximal attainable signal-to-noise ratio. We provide additional numerical evidence, suggesting that the magnitude of the improvement strongly depends on the amount and type of the stored, classical information. These results establish feedback as a potentially essential ingredient in pushing the fundamental limits of timekeeping in the quantum regime.

candidates.abstract: Federated learning lets multiple parties train a shared model without pooling their data, but a client with far less data than the others can end up poorly served even when the group's average accuracy looks fine. Lower-perplexity backbones consistently produced larger gains for the worst-performing client, with a rank correlation of -0.87 across nine dataset-backbone pairs; a backbone held out of the analysis confirmed the pattern. Personalization with Ditto recovered only 4-12% of the gap between training alone and full federation, and removing aggregation entirely erased the benefit. A client's update also showed no sign of conflicting with the group's update; the two are close to orthogonal, ruling out one proposed explanation for this failure. Practically: measure perplexity on a sample of task text before choosing a backbone, and do not rely on personalization to protect a data-poor client. candidates.title: All You Need Is Non-Commutative Words
candidates.abstract: We represent lexical tokens as unitary matrices and encode each sentence as their ordered product. candidates.title: Ensemble Diversity Optimization for Subjective Supervision
candidates.abstract: Subjective NLP tasks often exhibit systematic annotator disagreement, requiring models that represent uncertainty rather than collapse it. We introduce Ensemble Diversity Optimization (EDO), a prediction-space framework that jointly optimizes ensemble weights, effective cardinality, and calibration through a unified differentiable objective. EDO learns ensemble composition and size end-to-end via Gumbel-Softmax relaxation and incorporates a signed diversity regularizer, tuned on validation data, to steer optimization toward either preserving or suppressing disagreement. This regularization prevents ensemble collapse and enables controlled navigation of the utility-calibration trade-off. The framework integrates a soft F1 surrogate, class-weighted cross-entropy to address imbalance, and reliability-weighted diversity to regulate intra-ensemble variability. Experiments on four subjective text-classification benchmarks (ArMIS, ConvAbuse, HS-Brexit, MD-Agreement) show that EDO substantially improves probabilistic calibration, reducing cross-entropy (40-78% depending on baseline) and lowering Brier scores relative to Soft-CE, Soft-MD, Top-5 Voting, and WEL, while maintaining competitive F1 and better alignment with annotator distributions. These results demonstrate that jointly optimizing ensemble structure with a signed diversity regularizer provides an efficient, model-agnostic approach for modeling human subjectivity in supervised learning.

candidates.title: Fractional neural attention for efficient multiscale sequence processing
candidates.abstract: Attention mechanisms underpin the computational power of Transformer models, which have achieved remarkable success across diverse domains. Empirically, FNA achieves competitive text-classification performance even with a single layer and a single head; it also improves performance in image processing and neural machine translation. Finally, the diffusion map algorithm from geometric harmonics enables dimensionality reduction of FNA weights while preserving the intrinsic structure of embeddings and hidden states. candidates.title: SliceMoE: Routing Embedding Slices Instead of Tokens for Fine-Grained and Balanced Transformer Scaling
candidates.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers scale transformers by routing tokens to a sparse subset of feed-forward experts. A d-dimensional embedding is partitioned into S slices, and for each slice, a lightweight shared router predicts the top-k experts. Experts operate on their assigned slices independently, and outputs are reassembled, maintaining per-token FLOP efficiency. Because slices from different tokens interleave within an expert, utilization is naturally smoother. We propose a slice-level capacity loss, cross-slice dropout, and efficient fused batched GEMM kernels. candidates.title: Sample, Mix, or Verify? Allocating Test-Time Compute under Imperfect Verifiers
candidates.abstract: A common way to make language models and agents more accurate is to spend more compute at inference time: generate many candidate solutions and submit the one a verifier prefers. Success then requires that some candidate is correct and that the verifier picks it. The first grows predictably with the number of samples; the second does not, because real verifiers (unit tests, majority votes, LLM judges, reward models) accept wrong answers, reject right ones, and make correlated mistakes. With a fixed budget, a practitioner must decide how many samples to draw, which models to draw them from, and how much to spend on verification, and today these choices are made by rules of thumb. We introduce SPLIT, which makes them from a small labelled pilot. It rests on an exact formula for the probability of submitting a correct answer under accept/reject and top-score selection that accounts for varying task difficulty, blind spots shared across models, and correlated repeated verifier calls. SPLIT fits the formula by empirical Bayes and uses it to plan budgets on unseen tasks. Across seven benchmarks spanning math, science QA, code and software-engineering agents, 26 models, 175 agent systems and six kinds of real verifiers, all from public releases, SPLIT lands within 0.02-0.8 percentage points of the best allocation in hindsight, while every fixed rule we test loses at least 2.5 points in some setting. Regret depends only on how well SPLIT ranks configurations, and it stays near-optimal under compute, price and latency costs and online. The formula also explains when asking more LLM judges lowers precision. As a forecaster far beyond the pilot, SPLIT beats power-law fitting when the verifier caps success, and we report where it loses.

candidates.title: HEPTABench: A framework for portable and controlled agentic evaluations in high energy physics

candidates.title: An Optical KV Cache Network for Disaggregated LLM Serving
candidates.abstract: In disaggregated LLM serving, each request's KV cache moves from a prefill GPU to a decode GPU before the response begins, and a coding-agent turn often moves the KV cache of its whole long context. Behind an oversubscribed packet fabric, this transfer adds to the time to first token (TTFT). An optical circuit switch (OCS) can give every transfer a full-rate circuit for less than an oversubscribed packet fabric costs, but a mechanical OCS needs tens of milliseconds to reconfigure. We hide this delay inside the prefill. A reservation scheduler commits each circuit while the prefill is still computing, so the circuit is ready when the KV cache is, and each GPU reaches the OCS through its own wavelength-multiplexed (WDM) optics on one fiber pair. In simulations of GPU clusters on real serving traces with prefill times measured on H100 GPUs, this optical KV cache network matches 400G packet fabrics with adaptive routing at 0.55 to 0.78 times the cost of a 2:1 fabric and tolerates the 50 ms reconfiguration delay of a 384-port mechanical OCS.

candidates.title: Humans vs. Machines: A Comparison With AI Agents in Software Reverse Engineering
candidates.abstract: Can an autonomous AI agent reverse engineer a binary as well as a skilled human analyst? Do they adopt the same strategy, and can agents scale to real-world programs? We compare human and LLM-based software reverse engineering (SRE): nine models tackle two compact static-analysis challenges previously solved by human analysts, scored with a common understanding rubric, and we record their complete interactions with IDA Pro. This lets us compare not only what humans and agents recover, but also how they investigate a binary. The best agents (GPT-5.5 Pro, Claude Opus 4.8, and Kimi K3) achieve statistically human-competitive understanding on both tasks, while weaker models remain far behind. Ablations show that the gap depends on code representation and workflow demands, not on model capability alone: open-weight models improve substantially with richer code representations, whereas frontier models show no significant change. Similar success rates hide different workflows. Humans repeatedly revisit functions and follow local program structure; strong agents jump across the binary, retrieve information broadly, and rarely return to inspected code, a behavior we call greedy fetching. This strategy is not fixed: given semantically richer code, agents fetch less without losing understanding. Because greedy fetching aggregates large amounts of code in the agent's context, we measure context-window saturation across 4,000 real-world binaries: large windows accommodate many programs, but larger applications and lower-level representations quickly exhaust them. Autonomous reverse engineering is becoming competitive, with a large speed advantage, but scaling it will require better navigation, selective retrieval, and persistent analysis state, not merely larger context windows.

candidates.title: GeoScaffold: Learning Compact Geometric Latents via Reconstruction for Efficient Vision-Language Navigation
candidates.abstract: Recent vision-and-language navigation (VLN) systems increasingly adopt streaming Video-LLM policies that map egocentric RGB observations and instructions directly to low-level actions. This supervision turns the query states into compact geometric latents for action decoding, and through the shared weights also internalizes geometry into the backbone's own representations. Like a scaffold, the tokenizer, target generators, and reconstruction heads are discarded after training, leaving the backbone and action interface unchanged. Extensive experiments show that GeoScaffold consistently outperforms leading vision-only navigators on continuous VLN benchmarks, offering a practical paradigm for lightweight edge deployment of spatially aware embodied navigation models.

candidates.title: TANDEM: Task and Motion Planning with As-Needed Demonstrations for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model Fine-tuning

candidates.title: BLUE: Semantics-Preserving Video Compression for Efficient Vision-Language Surveillance Analytics
candidates.abstract: Continuous surveillance video creates a growing storage, transmission, and inference burden for enterprise video analytics systems. candidates.title: Attention-Free and Lightweight Token Reduction for Efficient Vision-Language Models
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance in multimodal understanding, yet remain challenging to deploy on resource-constrained edge devices due to the substantial computational overhead of processing numerous visual tokens. candidates.title: Reasoning-aware Speculative Decoding for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models in Autonomous Driving
candidates.abstract: Modern Vision-Language-Action (VLA) planners for autonomous driving emit a chain-of-causation (CoC) reasoning step \emph{before} producing a trajectory. The reasoning is autoregressive and dominates inference latency, while the trajectory head is parallel and cheap. Latency is an operational constraint in autonomous driving, so accelerating the reasoning step is the central problem we address. We observe that CoC reasoning has two qualitatively different needs: most tokens continue routine setup that follows naturally from the ego-trajectory history, and a small fraction encode commitments that require fresh visual evidence about an unexpected situation. We split this reasoning into two specialized paths: a \emph{routine reasoner} that handles the predictable continuation by attending to trajectory history, and a \emph{deliberative reasoner} (the unmodified VLA target) that handles novel cases by attending to current visual evidence, using the speculative decoding framework as the architectural template for how the two paths cooperate. Unlike standard speculative decoding, our routine reasoner is not a smaller replica of the target; the two reasoners are deliberately specialized to read different parts of the prompt. We propose two techniques to realize this. First, we introduce \textbf{FlatRoPE}, a 1D rotary positional embedding in the draft that breaks the rotational symmetry of the target's 3D M-RoPE, redirecting attention away from visual tokens and onto trajectory-history tokens. Second, we introduce \textbf{Action-aware RL (AARL)}, a post-training stage that uses an action-quality reward together with a static-reference KL anchor. Together, our two-reasoner system reduces the reasoning-step running time by approximately $4\times$ relative to the original Alpamayo planner.

candidates.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) map visual inputs into dense token sequences, imposing a quadratic computational bottleneck for inference. candidates.title: SUPRA-TEX: 3D Generation with Super-Aligned Texture
candidates.abstract: Single image 3D generation aims to dress a given 3D mesh with relightable materials while faithfully preserving the visual details of a reference image. Existing methods either introduce artifacts when fusing inconsistent multi-view predictions or struggle to preserve fine details through implicit image-feature conditioning. To resolve these challenges, we introduce SUPRA-Tex, built on the principle of decoupling visible-material estimation, surface alignment, and observation-guided 3D completion. This division of labor allows the 3D generator, trained on limited 3D data, to focus its capacity on preserving visible evidence and completing unobserved surfaces. Specifically, we first train an MLLM-based image editing model to predict lighting-separated PBR maps in the reference view. We then project these maps onto the visible surface and encode them with the pretrained material VAE encoder into native observation latents that share the generation target's latent space. An interleaved flow transformer holds these latents as fixed, read-only anchors while alternating unobserved-region and full-surface updates to generate complete material latents. This design achieves super-alignment with the reference, delivering What You See Is What You Get fidelity on visible regions and coherent completion on unobserved surfaces. Trained solely on public datasets, SUPRA-Tex achieves SOTA performance in both geometry-conditioned texturing and end-to-end asset generation, matching or even exceeding leading commercial systems on in-the-wild images. candidates.title: FlowState: Execution State as Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
candidates.abstract: Long-horizon tasks require LLM agents to continually draw on information from earlier interactions. However, retaining the full history increases context costs, while compressing it risks losing details needed later, and the relevance of historical information often becomes apparent as the task progresses. To address these challenges, we propose FlowState, which treats execution state as memory that can be retained and revisited across requests, unifying current decision-making with the reuse of historical information. FlowState preserves semantically typed state nodes, their relations, and references to raw tool observations, separating persistent retention from on-demand access. Within a single execution loop, Incremental State Update (ISU) maintains the current state based on new inputs and feedback, while Progressive State Access (PSA) progressively reveals historical states and supporting evidence as needed during reasoning. Together, these mechanisms enable agents to reassess prior decisions in light of new information and guide subsequent actions. Compared with a full-context baseline using the same DeepSeek-V4-Flash model, FlowState improves the average success rate on MemoryArena and the average pass rate on τ^3-Bench by 4.55 and 13.95 percentage points, respectively, while reducing total token consumption by 43.2% and 40.6%. These results demonstrate the performance and efficiency advantages of FlowState on long-horizon tasks.

candidates.title: Evaluating Agentic Capabilities Before Post-Training: An End-to-End Approach
candidates.abstract: Agentic capabilities are increasingly important for modern LLMs, yet remain difficult to evaluate during pretraining. Existing approaches typically rely on static trajectory-derived tasks or likelihood-based proxies, which are lightweight but provide limited visibility into how base models behave in interactive environments. We introduce ASAP (Agent Scaffold Adaptation for Pretraining Evaluation), a lightweight framework for eliciting and evaluating agentic behavior from pretrained base models on end-to-end tasks. Rather than converting base models into chat-style agents, ASAP preserves the completion interface and adapts existing agent scaffolds through structured trajectory continuation, short reference prefixes, and minimal recovery mechanisms. Across software-engineering and deep-research benchmarks, ASAP yields discriminative end-to-end performance across base models and pretraining checkpoints. Beyond aggregate scores, ASAP exposes model-generated execution trajectories, enabling analysis of exploration, editing, testing, recovery, and task completion across training stages. These trajectories provide a behavioral view of how agent-relevant capabilities change during pretraining and how execution patterns differ after post-training. Our results suggest that end-to-end agent evaluation can complement conventional pretraining benchmarks by providing a practical diagnostic of interactive model behavior.
